"I sent several invitations to dignitaries in Estelore requesting their attendance," Philander muses. "I never received a reply... I remember being miffed at them discounting the discoveries of someone they must imagine a backwater hedge-mage." "Don't get sidetracked, Ander," Ria snaps. "Please, continue." "As the most powerful wraith in the pack, I had first pick of the spread that was the convocation, and the two of you happened to be the most tantalising morsels. There's no way to put it lightly: I murdered you. I ripped your souls from your bodies, tore them like fruit off the bough... you had a flavor that was quite overwhelming. And then when I realized what I'd done, I regretted it. "Regret is a strange sensation, especially when it's the first emotion that you've ever experienced. I don't know if there was something special about both your souls that made you different from the thousands I'd consumed up to that point, or if you were simply the final ones that pushed me across some heretofore unknown threshold. But looking down at your half-eaten souls, all I knew was what I'd just done, what I'd been doing was wrong." "I..." Ander looks over himself, perhaps expecting to be missing a limb or his tail. "This is all a lot to take in." "Even for all that I am, I can't turn back time, undo what's been done; only set things right. As the other wraiths continued feasting on what was left of the Convocation of Mirrors, I destroyed and devoured them one by one as they lay helpless in their stupor, then saved the only two souls that still remained remotely intact through all this — you. Even then, that wasn't enough: I've been with Tychris since, trying to make up for what happened those two and a half centuries ago. I've been keeping the both of you here... well, Philander's magic is one thing, but really, it's to remind myself of what I've done, and perhaps through offering you some kind of eternal comfort, make up for it all. "Eventually, I came to understand that there were others like me... awakened to a new reality, the reality of this world and the perspective its inhabitants had given us. While there were some disagreements, we all concurred that what we had been doing was wrong, and that we needed to help the natives against our own kind." Ander grimaces. "I'm beginning to see where this is going..." "The natives worshipped local deities... gods that perhaps might once have existed to provoke belief in them, but had long since left this world if they ever were here. By good fate or good fortune, the number of us awakened were seven... we believed the natives would be more accepting of our help if we took the guises of their gods and leveraged that familiarity to avoid uncomfortable situations." "So," Ria says, her arms folded. "You're not really Nareva." "Am I? I was nothing before, a creature without a personality or name. Everyone calls me Nareva, I perform all the functions within Nareva's domain. I think of myself as Nareva. At what point is it sufficient to say that there is no difference between a mask and the one who wears it? "And more importantly, knowing all this, what are you going to do about it, if anything?"'

rows.original: More silence. Ander and Ria look at each other, then down at the ground. "We're already dead," Ander mutters, defeated. "There's not much we can do at this point. Ria?" "I... I don't know, either. I should try to strangle you for murdering us, witch, but looking at you now, I'm not sure I can find it in me to lay hands on you." A sigh from Nareva. "Actual compassion. A rare virtue, more common in the past but less so in the en Tychris line of today, considering how it's degenerated." "What do you mean, degenerated?" Ria demands. Of all of Nareva's revelations thus far, this appears to have hit her the hardest; with her hands on the back of her head, her body bowed, nothing remains of Ria's confident warrioress demeanour. "Ah. Well. While the Lord Evander en Tychris is quite formidable in a sense, he's nothing like you, Phyria en Tychris. Short. Weak. Brittle-boned. Prone to poor health... and continually amazing the Marches by not just surviving to his majority, but actually managing to father an heir on the Lady Tethys en Tychris. Easier to yield in the face of pain. Similarly, you are nothing like the founding stock of your line; the thinning of your blood began even before the wraiths ever came to this world. What was the saying? 'Good times create weak men'? Tychris was a victim of its own success; comfort, indulgences and riches have a tendency to encourage people to stop thinking with the head on their shoulders and with their... other heads." Ander looks appropriately chastised at that. "However, the aftereffects of the Godswar hastened the downward spiral. With both heir and spare dead, an attempt was made to consolidate what lands remained under the various branches of the family through consanguineous marriages. It worked, but at the price of considerable inbreeding; sickly and malformed offspring — by their ancestors' standards, anyway — plagued the line for generations afterwards. Those newborns who didn't die outright were otherwise defective, and the en Tychris were forced to accept those heirs. Once their position was relatively secure, they needed — and still need — political alliances with the heartlands, which watered down the blood even further as they were forced to take the leftover sons and daughters of what used to be Belhar. Afterwards — " Ria screams, a horrible, primal sound that echoes through the temple, her hands pressed over her ears. "No more! I — I don't want this!" Nareva shrugs. "Then you should be careful not to ask questions you're not ready to receive the answers to. If it's any consolation, the descendants of your line made decisions that were the most sensible at the time; the price they had to pay was comfortably distant enough in the future that none of them ever considered it. Paying for the now with tomorrow, as it were." "Sister, I — " Ria whirls on Ander, tears in her eyes as she grabs him by the throat. "It's all your fault, you pompous prig! If we hadn't been away from home, we could've fought back! We could've lived, set things right, instead of playing at your stupid convocation and killing — no, death would've been better than this slow decay, not quite alive, not dead yet!" Quietly, Nareva shifts her eyes. "Technically, it's my — " "No, it's not your fault. Now I get why I'm not inclined to try and kill you, witch; if you're not lying and you didn't have a heart before you ate all of us, then I can't blame a beast for doing what a beast does, it doesn't know good from evil." Slowly, Ria takes a deep breath and forces herself to let go of her brother. "If you're really regretful of what you did... can't you restore the line? While all this was going on, couldn't you have intervened to save the house of Tychris?" "I could," Nareva agrees, "but there wouldn't be much point. The spark, the will, the flame that animates them — it's gone. Restoring their bodies would do little to revive their spirits, and without the latter the former would be akin to giving a child a sword she's unable to lift. If the line finds it in them to pull through this crisis intact, I'll consider it." Ander scowls, rubbing his sore neck. "Her words make sense, sister. If things were already that bad, coddling them wouldn't have solved anything. It'd only have masked the rot until the stench grew too thick to conceal, perhaps even accelerated the decline." "Big words, considering it probably started with you and your fondness for dream-orgies." Ria's face hardens, her body tensing. She's clearly unsure about something, yet determined to see it through. "You know what, Nareva or whoever you are? I changed my mind; I don't want to go just yet, not while I've still got unfinished business. Not while knowing that Tychris is such a mess as it is. You're supposed to be a god, isn't there any way I can get back and help set things right?" Nareva considers the question, rubbing her chin. "This is... unprecedented. Difficult, to be sure; but I think I have a solution that will work. And what about you, Ander? What will you do now?" "If Ria can find it in herself to stay, I'd be remiss if I left without her." "Good. Would you be so kind as to introduce [pc.name] to the workings of mirror magic while I attend to your sister's request?" Ria squints. "You're not going to pull a fast one on us, are you?" "You've agreed to stay for the time being. Unlike your brother, I know enough not to ruin a decent resolution to a conflict when I see one." While 'mander and goddess break out into a small discussion, Ander takes you by the shoulder and pulls you aside. "Come on, then. As much as Ria likes to argue, there's a lot we have to cover and I'd rather not have to rush over several important concepts." You shrug, and follow Ander away from the still-bickering duo and towards the center of the circle. Considering the situation the 'mander siblings are in, you can see why they're taking these revelations quite well — or at least, are appearing to. What's past is past... ...But what about you? How do you feel about all this? Knowing the gods are a lie, a mask, but when does the mask become the person wearing it? Was that truth worth it? Does it matter what they were before, in the light of what they've done and what they've become? Only you can know that... "[pc.name]?" "Sorry! I was lost in thought..." Ander looks at you, his gaze softening. "I suppose it's a lot for me to take in, too, but I'm going to need your undivided attention for the next few hours. Can you manage that?"
rows.translation: 更多的沉默。安德和莉亚对视了一眼，然后又将目轻型投向地面。 “我们已经完了，”安德沮丧地低声说道，“现在我们已经无能为力了。莉亚，你觉得呢？” “我……我也不知道。我…… 应该 那个女巫，他们本来想杀了你来为我们的死报仇，但现在看着你，我实在想不出自己是否有勇气动手部。” 纳雷瓦叹了口气：“真正的同情心啊……这种美德已经十分罕见了。在过去它还比较普遍，但到了如今的恩·提克里斯家族，这种品质已经变得十分稀少，因为这个家族已经堕落了。” “你是什么意思…… 退化了的？”莉亚问道。在纳雷瓦迄今为止透露的所有信息中，这一条似乎对她的打击最大；她双手部抱头，身体弯曲，那副自信勇敢的女战士形象早已荡然无存。 啊，嗯……虽然埃万德·恩·提克里斯大人确实相当强大，但他根本比不上你，菲莉亚·恩·提克里斯。他个子矮小，体弱多病，骨骼脆弱……然而，他竟然奇迹般地在成年之后活了下来，甚至还为泰西斯·恩·提克里斯夫人生下了一个继承人，这让边境地区的人民感到十分惊讶。 在痛苦面前，人更容易屈服。同样，你也与你这一血脉的起源毫无关系；你的血液开始变得稀薄，甚至早在那些邪灵降临这个世界之前就已经开始了。有句俗话说得没错：“安逸的环境会造就懦弱的人”。 提克里斯成为了自己成功的牺牲品；舒适的生活、享乐以及财富往往会让人不再用理智去思考问题，而是…… 其他 好吧。” 安德听后显得确实受到了应有的惩戒。 “然而，神战带来的后果加速了这种衰败的趋势。由于继承人和备选继承人都去世了，人们便试图通过近亲婚姻来巩固家族各个分支手部中剩余的土地。 这一方法确实奏效了，但代价却是严重的近亲繁殖——按照他们祖先的标准，那些出生后体弱多病、畸形畸变的后代困扰了这个家族数代人。那些没有立即夭折的新生儿也都有各种缺陷，因此恩·提克里斯家族不得不接受这些后代作为自己的继承者。 一旦他们的地位相对稳固，他们就需要——而且至今仍然需要——与那些核心地区建立政治联盟。这种联盟使得他们的血统进一步稀释，因为他们不得不接纳那些曾经属于贝尔哈尔地区的残余子孙。 之后—— 莉亚发出了凄厉的尖叫，那是一种令人毛骨悚然的、原始的叫声，在寺庙中回荡着，她双手部紧紧捂住自己的耳朵。“不要再这样了！我……我再也不想经历这些了！” 纳雷瓦耸了耸肩：“那么，你就应该小心，不要去问那些你还没有准备好接受答案的问题。 如果这能让你感到些许安慰的话，你的后代们在当时所做的决定确实是当时最明智的选择；他们所付出的代价在未来的时间跨度里显得足够遥远，以至于他们中的没有人会去考虑这些代价。可以说，他们是用未来的代价来换取现在的利益。" 姐姐，我——” 莉亚猛地转向安德，眼中含着泪水，一把抓住他的喉咙：“一切都…… 你的 错就错在你这个自大的蠢货！如果我们没有离开家，我们就能够反抗了！我们本可以活下来，把事情纠正过来，而不是参加你那愚蠢的集会，最后导致死亡——不， 死亡 这本该比这种缓慢的衰败要好得多——既不算真正活着，又还没完全死去！” 纳雷瓦轻轻移开了视线。“从技术上来说，它…… 我的 不，这不是你的错。现在我明白为什么我并不想杀你这个女巫了；如果你没有说谎，而且在吞噬我们所有人之前你确实没有心……那么，我就不能责怪一只野兽做出它该做的事了，毕竟它分不清善恶。”莉亚缓缓深吸一口气，强迫自己放开弟弟的手部。“如果你真的对自己所做的事感到后悔……难道就不能恢复那条血脉吗？在这一切发生的时候，你难道不能出手部拯救提克里斯家族吗？ 我可以，”纳雷瓦同意道，“但那样也没什么意义。驱动他们的那股力量、那份意志、那团点燃他们生命的火焰——都已经消失了。恢复他们的肉体并不能重新唤醒他们的精神，而没有精神，肉体也就如同给一个根本举不起剑的孩子一把剑而已。如果他们能够凭借自己的力量安然度过这场危机，那我才会考虑这个办法。 安德皱着眉头，揉着疼痛的脖子说道：“姐姐，她的话有道理。如果情况已经那么糟糕了，一味地娇惯他们根本解决不了任何问题，只会让问题暂时被掩盖起来，直到恶臭变得无法忍受，甚至可能会加速事情的恶化。 说得好听，不过这一切很可能都是你一手部造成的，毕竟你那么热衷于那些疯狂的派对吧。”莉亚的表情变得严肃起来，全身也变得紧绷起来。她显然对某些事情感到不确定，但依然决心要把事情解决到底。“你知道吗，纳雷瓦，或者无论你到底是谁……我改变主意了，我现在还不想离开，至少在我还有未完成的事情之前，至少在知道提克里斯还处于这种混乱状态的时候。你本来应该是个神明啊，难道就没有办法让我回去帮忙把事情弄好吗？ 纳雷瓦沉思着，用手部摩着下巴：“这……确实是前所未有的情况。当然，解决起来会很有难度；但我想我有一个可行的办法。那么你呢，安德？你现在打算怎么做？ 好的。请您介绍一下吧。 [pc.name] 在我处理你妹妹的事情的同时，你能不能也解释一下镜像魔法的工作原理呢？” 莉亚眯起了眼睛：“你该不会想骗我们吧？” “你们已经同意暂时留下来帮忙了。和你的哥哥不同，我懂得如何把握时机，不会在看到一个即将解决的冲突时，破坏它。当“曼德尔和女神开始小声争论时，安德尔抓住你的肩膀，将你拉到一边。“走吧，虽然莉亚喜欢争论，但我们还有很多事情需要讨论，我可不想匆忙地讲解几个重要的概念。你耸了耸肩，跟着安德离开了那对仍在争吵的两人，朝着圆圈的中心走去。考虑到“曼德尔兄妹”目前所处的处境，你就明白为什么他们对这些真相反应如此平静了——至少表面上是这样。 过去的就让它过去吧…… 但是你呢？你对这一切有什么感受？ 既然知道那些神明只是谎言，只是面具，那么，究竟在什么时候，这个面具才会真正成为戴着它的人本身呢？ 这样的真相，真的值得吗？ 鉴于他们曾经的所作所为以及如今已经成为什么样的人，他们过去是什么样的人，这真的重要吗？ 只有你自己才最清楚……[pc.name]对不起！我刚才走神了……” 安德看着你，他的目轻型变得柔和起来。“我想，对于我来说，这些信息也确实有点难以消化。但在接下来的几个小时里，我需要你全神贯注地听我说。你能做到吗？

rows.original: Ria's right — this is madness. Both she and Ander are in no frame of mind to argue for their freedom right now; with how heated things are, they'll only worsen the situation. "...You're treating us like tools!" Ander currently has an accusatory finger levelled straight at Nareva, who's taking the accusation with an air of sad forbearance. The prince clearly isn't used to people denying him, and doesn't look like he's taking it well. "Is that so?" the goddess purrs. "If I'd thought you a tool, Ander, you'd be much less than you are now. Tools don't have emotions. They don't cry, they don't laugh, they don't get upset. Tools don't have a will of their own. If I'd wanted to reduce you to a tool, Philander en Tychris... you wouldn't even have the self-awareness to know it." Ander shakes his head, opens his mouth to speak, but you decide that it's time for you to step in and right the situation. He looks a little surprised at your entrance, taking an involuntary half-step back as you place yourself between him and Nareva, then Ria pulls him off the field completely with a hissing whisper of words you don't quite catch. "Well then, another contender takes up arms and steps forth," Nareva says, levelling her dark gaze upon you. "Unless I'm mistaken as to your intentions, [pc.race]." "No, you're right. I intend to plead their case," you reply. "And a good thing, too. Philander here may be clever, but he's also been utterly spoiled by his royal father. He's quite surprised that I'm not particularly swayed by his brand of sophistic argumentation, which basically amounts to several variants of 'do you know who I am?' Quite droll, really." "I hope to provide more of a challenge, then. Will you free the siblings?" Nareva chuckles. "I'll repeat myself: no. As the goddess of knowledge, magic and secrets, it is entirely within my purview to preserve Ander and Ria here within my dream. Furthermore, this stretches beyond my portfolio; as the patron deity of Tychris, I feel that I have a responsibility to preserve what I can of it, even in its senescence. The city and house of Tychris will crumble someday; nothing lasts forever. However, in this fashion, at least some of Ander's achievements will be preserved. "Will you rebut my rationale for my actions, [pc.name]?" "Now? Not likely. But would you mind indulging me in a conversation?" "Of course. Let me make myself comfortable." Stretching lazily, Nareva winds her sinuous coils about herself and cups her chin in her hands, her elbows planted on her serpentine body. "In the Dream, if nowhere else... we have time." [pc.cunningRange 60 |The goddess appears pretty composed here... just waiting for her to slip up and make a gaffe isn't going to work. If you just keep silent all the time, she's going to consider the conversation done and cut it off. Seems like you'll have to fight for every scrap of useful information out of Nareva, provoke her into defending herself so she'll be more inclined to talk. ] [pc.cunningRange 80 |On the other hand, you're not going to get anywhere by throwing about wild accusations like Ander or Ria would have — if you're going to say something, it should be at least reasonably plausible... ]
rows.translation: 莉亚说得对——这简直太疯狂了。现在她和安德都完全没有心情去为自己的自由争论；在这种紧张的气氛下，他们只会让事情变得更糟。 “……你们把我们当成了工具！”安德指责道，他的手部指直直地指向纳雷瓦，而纳雷瓦则带着一种无奈和悲哀的表情接受了这一指责。 这位王子显然不习惯别人拒绝他，而且看起来他对此反应不佳。 “是吗？”女神轻声说道，“如果我认为你只是个工具，安德，你的地位现在也不会这么高。工具是不会有情感的。 他们不会哭泣，不会大笑，也不会感到沮丧。工具本身是没有意志的。如果我真的想把你变成一个工具，菲兰德·恩·提克里斯……你甚至都不会有自我意识去察觉到这一点。 安德摇摇头，张开嘴想要说话，但你决定现在是时候介入并扭转这个局面了。 当你站在他和纳雷瓦之间时，他看起来有些惊讶，不由自主地向后退了半步。随后，莉亚用一些你听不太清的低语声将他完全从场地上拉走了。 那么，又有一位竞争者拿起了武器，站了出来，”纳雷瓦说道，她那深色的目光直直地盯着你。“除非我误解了你的意图…… [pc.race]不，你说得对。我确实打算为他们辩护。”你回答道。 “这倒也是件好事。虽然菲兰德挺聪明的，但他也被他的王室父亲宠坏了。他很惊讶我并没有被他那种花招百出的论证方式所影响——那些论证基本上都只是在重复‘你知道我是谁吗？’这句话而已。真是挺可笑的。” “那么，我希望自己能带来更大的挑战。你会释放那对兄妹吗？” 纳雷瓦轻笑了一声。 我再重复一遍：不行。作为知识、魔法与秘密的女神，将安德和莉亚留在我的梦境中完全属于我的职责范围。此外，这不仅仅是我个人的责任；作为提克里斯的庇护神，我觉得我有责任尽我所能去保护这一切，哪怕它已经变得破败不堪。提克里斯的城市和宅邸终有一天会消失；没有什么是永恒的。但是，通过这种方式，至少安德的一些成就能够被保留下来。 你愿意反驳我为自己所采取的行动所给出的理由吗？ [pc.name]现在吗？不太可能吧。不过，你愿意陪我聊一会儿吗？” “当然可以。让我先找个舒服的位置坐下来吧。”纳雷瓦懒洋洋地伸了个懒腰，将自己那蜿蜒曲折的身体盘绕在身上，双手部托着下巴，肘部撑在身躯上。“至少在梦中……我们有的是时间。 [pc.cunningRange 60 |这位女神在这里表现得相当镇定自若……仅仅等着她犯错或说错话是行不通的。如果你一直保持沉默，她就会认为谈话已经结束，从而停止交谈。看来，你必须设法从娜雷瓦那里获取每一条有用的信息，激怒她让她进行辩解，这样她才更有可能开口说话。 ] [pc.cunningRange 80 |另一方面，如果你像安德或莉亚那样随意抛出一些毫无根据的指控，是根本不会有什么结果的。如果你真的要说什么的话，至少应该让这些说法显得有些可信才对…… ]
rows.raw: " Ria's right — this is madness. Both she and Ander are in no frame of mind to argue for their freedom right now; with how heated things are, they'll only worsen the situation. "...You're treating us like tools!" Ander currently has an accusatory finger levelled straight at Nareva, who's taking the accusation with an air of sad forbearance. The prince clearly isn't used to people denying him, and doesn't look like he's taking it well. "Is that so?" the goddess purrs. "If I'd thought you a tool, Ander, you'd be much less than you are now. Tools don't have emotions. They don't cry, they don't laugh, they don't get upset. Tools don't have a will of their own. If I'd wanted to reduce you to a tool, Philander en Tychris... you wouldn't even have the self-awareness to know it." Ander shakes his head, opens his mouth to speak, but you decide that it's time for you to step in and right the situation. He looks a little surprised at your entrance, taking an involuntary half-step back as you place yourself between him and Nareva, then Ria pulls him off the field completely with a hissing whisper of words you don't quite catch. "Well then, another contender takes up arms and steps forth," Nareva says, levelling her dark gaze upon you. "Unless I'm mistaken as to your intentions, [pc.race]." "No, you're right. I intend to plead their case," you reply. "And a good thing, too. Philander here may be clever, but he's also been utterly spoiled by his royal father. He's quite surprised that I'm not particularly swayed by his brand of sophistic argumentation, which basically amounts to several variants of 'do you know who I am?' Quite droll, really." "I hope to provide more of a challenge, then. Will you free the siblings?" Nareva chuckles. "I'll repeat myself: no. As the goddess of knowledge, magic and secrets, it is entirely within my purview to preserve Ander and Ria here within my dream. Furthermore, this stretches beyond my portfolio; as the patron deity of Tychris, I feel that I have a responsibility to preserve what I can of it, even in its senescence. The city and house of Tychris will crumble someday; nothing lasts forever. However, in this fashion, at least some of Ander's achievements will be preserved. "Will you rebut my rationale for my actions, [pc.name]?" "Now? Not likely. But would you mind indulging me in a conversation?" "Of course. Let me make myself comfortable." Stretching lazily, Nareva winds her sinuous coils about herself and cups her chin in her hands, her elbows planted on her serpentine body. "In the Dream, if nowhere else... we have time." If you just keep silent all the time, she's going to consider the conversation done and cut it off. Seems like you'll have to fight for every scrap of useful information out of Nareva, provoke her into defending herself so she'll be more inclined to talk. ] [pc.cunningRange 80 |On the other hand, you're not going to get anywhere by throwing about wild accusations like Ander or Ria would have — if you're going to say something, it should be at least reasonably plausible... ]"

rows.original:
"Of course I can," Nareva replies, looking rather pleased with herself. "In fact, it's one of my favorite topics. While I always had a slight edge over the rest of the Seven because of the en Tychris line being vocal advocates of wizardry and learning, it wasn't till during the Godswar that I was formally adopted as patron of the royal line and indeed, the city-state itself. Before then, only those like the prince and his students cared very much about my existence and worship."

        "Is that so?"
        
        "Tychris was in a precarious position, you see. Unfortunately, Prince Telandros had lost both his heir and a daughter in one fell swoop, the queen was inconsolable, and to make things worse, a host of otherworldly monsters and their enthralled minions was marching up from the coastlands. Oh, and as a result of that, the glass trade from which Tychris derived much of its revenue collapsed overnight, because people concerned with not being monster prey don't care much for fine glass. Faced with a dismal future from a potentially world-ending threat, your royal parents were more than happy to receive me when I incarnated and informed them I was obliged to give them my aid."
        
        Ria glowers. "You used a crisis to worm your way into Father's confidence!"

“是吗？”

“你知道，提克里斯当时处于一个非常危险的境地。不幸的是，泰兰德罗斯王子在一次事件中失去了自己的继承人和女儿，王后悲痛欲绝，而更糟糕的是，一群来自异世界的怪物以及它们那些被控制的仆从正从沿海地区向这里进军。 哦，正因为如此，提克里斯的主要收入来源——玻璃贸易在一夜之间就崩溃了，因为那些担心自己会成为怪物猎物的人根本不会对精美的玻璃感兴趣。面对这种可能带来世界末日的威胁，当我的灵魂转世后向你的王室父母说明自己有义务帮助他们时，他们自然非常高兴地接受了我的帮助。蕾亚怒目而视：“你利用这场危机来赢得父亲的信任！

rows.original: "You say you're the patron deity of Tychris. Can you tell me more about that?"
rows.translation: 你说你是提克里斯的守护神，能告诉我更多关于这件事的吗？
rows.raw: '"You say you\'re the patron deity of Tychris. Can you tell me more about that?"'

rows.original:
"Like I said, the royal siblings had the misfortune to be consumed by a number of wraiths while they slept. Their students and servants, alas, suffered a similar fate."

        Ander grimaces. "Tell us, then! Tell us everything! I at least have a right to know how my sister and I perished!"
        
        "Ah-ah-ah. There you go again, Philander, making demands and turning away people who would otherwise be favorably disposed to you. You lord father was always worried that he'd spoiled you as a child, and blamed himself for allowing you to gallivant away from the city for your little convocation."
        
        "If you wouldn't try to change the subject on me..."
        
        Nareva's nonplussed as ever as she raises a finger to her lips. "I wouldn't need to calm things down if you didn't make demands as if this was Tychris Palace and I were but one of your maids out for a dalliance. You do understand your current position, yes?"
rows.translation:
正如我所说，那几位王室兄弟姐妹在睡梦中不幸被许多怨灵吞噬。他们的学生和仆从，也同样遭遇了同样的命运。”

安德皱起了眉头。“那么，快告诉我们吧！把一切都告诉我们！ 我至少有权知道我和妹妹究竟是怎么死的！”

“啊哈啊，又来这一套了，菲兰德。你总是提出各种要求，把那些本来会对你抱有好感的人吓跑。你那位自以为是的父亲，从小就担心自己会把你宠坏，还总是因为让你离开城市去参加那些小聚会而自责不已。如果你不试图转移我的注意力的话……”

纳雷瓦像往常一样有些不知所措，她把手指放在嘴唇上想了想：“如果你不像是在提克里斯宫里，而我只是你们那些出来寻欢作乐的女仆之一那样提出各种要求的话，我就不需要去平息这场纷争了。 你确实明白自己目前的处境，对吧？

rows.original:
Nareva chuckles at that and raises a finger to her plush lips. "Anyone can simply yell protests at fortissimo, my dear [pc.race] guest. If you're not going to behave any differently from either of the siblings, maybe I shouldn't be wasting my time here."

        Grr... she's right, though; you don't have enough information at this point. Surely the time will come when you've all your ducks lined up in a row and you can strike, but until then, you need to keep the goddess talking and learn more about the situation.
rows.translation:
纳雷瓦听到这话轻笑了一声，然后把一根手指放在自己柔软的嘴唇上说道：“亲爱的，任何人都可以用最大的音量大声抗议啊。 [pc.race] 客人：“如果你和那两个兄弟姐妹的行为没有任何不同，那我在这里浪费时间或许真的没有意义。”

哼……她说的没错，目前你确实掌握的信息还不够。总会有那么一天，当你把所有条件都准备妥当时，就可以采取行动了。但在那之前，你得让这位‘女神’继续开口说话，这样才能了解更多关于当前情况的细节。

rows.original: "This is wrong and you know it! You have no right to keep them here!"
rows.translation: 这是不对的，你心里明白这一点！你没有权利把它们留在这里！
rows.raw: '"This is wrong and you know it! You have no right to keep them here!"'

rows.original: You consider the goddess' words. "Obliged? That's an odd way to put it. If you became the city's patron deity beforehand, an obligation to protect them would make sense, but you said you found favor with the royal family during the Godswar. So, what was that obligation, if I might ask?" "You may. At the height of its power, Tychris was a center of learning, a rare thing in the Marches. The royal family were noted patrons of the arcane sciences, as the prince himself will attest, and while not as extensive as old Belhar they still managed a number of interesting discoveries in their time. It's the same decision I made with the royal siblings — it would be such a shame if their knowledge were to be lost forever, especially after how dedicated they were to advancing my cause. I merely wished to repay the favor, but gained so much more from it." Ander folds his arms. "So much more, you say." Nareva just smiles. "I gained the friendship of your bereaved father, Prince Philander en Tychris. I am a goddess; anything your parents could have given me, I could have easily created for myself. Save for one thing, that is — their companionship. Being a deity can be lonely at times; mortals in my presence are prone to either rage against me as you are doing now, or begin some kind of fervent worship or the other. It's nice to be able to just talk to someone from time to time." "And for all that you did, you allowed my family's legacy to fall into ruin." "Ah, that was my mistake. Like I said, Tychris was a victim of its own success before the Godswar; if I had simply coddled them, they would not have learned any lessons from the Godswar. Unfortunately... the judgement in error was mine. I underestimated the wraiths, and though the city-state was saved from destruction, it has not healed from their ravages. "Don't look so upset, prince. Without my intervention, Tychris would not even have survived, even in its diminished form. Things could be much worse."
rows.translation: 你仔细思考着这位女神的话语。“感到有义务？这种表达方式确实有些奇怪。如果你事先就成为了这座城市的守护神，那么保护这座城市确实是一种义务；但你说你在神战期间赢得了王室的青睐，那么这种‘义务’也就另当别论了。 那么，这个义务究竟是什么呢？我可以问一下吗？” “当然可以。在它的鼎盛时期，提克里斯成为了学术研究的中心，在边境地区这样的地方实属罕见。王室成员一直是神秘学的热心赞助者，正如那位王子本人所证明的那样。虽然他们的研究规模不如古老的贝尔哈尔，但在他们那个时代，仍然取得了一些有趣的成果。 这个决定和我当初为王室兄弟姐妹们所做的决定是一样的——结果也会是一样的。 这样的 如果他们的知识就这样永远消失，未免太可惜了，尤其是他们为推动我的事业付出了如此多的努力。我本来只是想报答他们的帮助，但却从中获得了更多的收获。 安德尔双臂交叉抱在胸前。 原来还有这么多啊。” 纳雷瓦只是微笑着回答：“我赢得了你那位已故父亲的友谊——菲兰德·恩·提克里斯王子。我是一位女神；你父母能够给予我的任何东西，我都可以轻易地为自己创造出来。 唯有一点除外，那就是他们的陪伴。身为神明，有时也会感到孤独；而当我出现在凡人面前时，他们要么会像你现在这样对我发怒，要么就会开始狂热地崇拜我。 能够偶尔和别人聊聊天，确实是一件很愉快的事情。” “而你所做的所有那些事，却让我的家族的传承陷入了毁灭。 啊，那确实是我的失误。正如我所说，在神战之前，提克里斯其实只是自己成功的受害者；如果我当时没有对他们过于纵容，他们就不会从那场神战中吸取任何教训。不幸的是……这个错误的判断确实出自我之手。我低估了那些幽灵的力量，虽然那个城邦最终没有遭到毁灭，但它至今仍未从那些灾难中恢复过来。 别这么难过，王子。如果没有我的干预，即使是变弱后的提克里斯，也根本活不下来。事情本可能会变得…… 很多 更糟的是……

rows.original:
"Ria's not wrong," you say. "It does appear that you used the impending crisis to install yourself quite firmly in House Tychris."

        "Ah, but appearances are easily deceiving, my young [pc.race]," Nareva replies. "You really should at least try to hear out a side completely before levelling accusations. They can be quite serious, after all, and one should have the facts beforehand to avoid embarrassment, don't you agree?"
        
        Ria interjects once more. "You admitted as much yourself! What else needs to be said?"
        
        A sigh. "Such the spitting image of your mother, in both appearance and temperament. You will learn, as she did, that while being forceful and overbearing works on courtiers and common soldiers, I am not as easily cowed. Here in my Dream, truth is not determined by how something makes you feel, nor how many voices are lent to it. Here, we deal with what can be proven, and I doubt you can prove your accusation.
        
        "Now with this lesson in mind, [pc.name], perhaps we should take this from the top again."
rows.translation:
莉亚说得没错，”你说，“看起来你确实利用这场即将到来的危机，让自己在提克里斯家族中占据了稳固的地位。”

“啊，但外表往往具有欺骗性，我的年轻人。 [pc.race]确实应该至少先听听另一方的解释，再轻易地提出指责，”纳雷瓦回答道。“毕竟，这些指责可能会相当严重，而事先了解事实才能避免尴尬，你不觉得吗？莉亚再次插话道：“你自己也承认了这一点！还有什么好说的呢？”

他叹了口气：“你在外貌和性格上简直和你母亲一模一样。你会像她一样明白：虽然我对朝臣和普通士兵来说可能显得强势而专横，但我可不会那么容易就被吓倒。 在我的梦想世界里，真相并不取决于某件事会让你产生怎样的感受，也不取决于有多少人支持这一观点。在这里，我们只关注那些可以被证实的事情，而我怀疑你无法证明自己的指控。

“现在，牢记这一道理…… [pc.name]或许我们应该从头开始重新考虑这个问题。

        A sigh. "Such the spitting image of your mother, in both appearance and temperament. You will learn, as she did, that while being forceful and overbearing works on courtiers and common soldiers, I am not as easily cowed. Here in my Dream, truth is not determined by how something makes you feel, nor how many voices are lent to it. Here, we deal with what can be proven, and I doubt you can prove your accusation.
        
        "Now with this lesson in mind, [pc.name], perhaps we should take this from the top again."'

rows.original:
You pause a moment, hoping to get a read on the situation and perhaps let Nareva continue talking, but Ria seizes the moment to interject herself into the conversation, quickly turning it into the beginnings of an argument. Thinning her lips ever so slightly, Nareva snaps her fingers, and Ria falls silent — or rather, her lips are moving but no sound emerges from her mouth.

        "It'll wear off after a minute or so, dear. Plenty of time to reconsider so rudely interrupting a conversation. Now then, [pc.name], where were we?"
rows.translation:
你停顿了片刻，试图弄清楚当前的局势，或许想让纳雷瓦继续说话，但莉亚却抓住这个机会插话进来，很快使得谈话变成了争吵的开始。纳雷瓦微微撇了撇嘴，打了个响指，莉亚立刻闭上了嘴——或者说，她的嘴唇还在动，但却没有发出任何声音。

“过一会儿这种感觉就会消失的，亲爱的。你还有足够的时间来考虑自己这样打断别人谈话是否合适。现在，让我们继续吧…… [pc.name]我们刚才说到哪里了？

rows.translation: 保持沉默，观察事态的发展。

rows.original:
"You're not wrong," Nareva agrees with a small sigh. "Still, there's no way for us to change the past, not even for the likes of me. Speculating endlessly on what could have been isn't going to get us anywhere, my dear guest, and I'd rather not dwell on what-ifs and could-have-beens that're merely thinly-veiled accusations."

        Grr... you've wasted time here, and probably made the situation worse to boot. You really should try to stick to the objective facts when going on the offense here.
rows.translation:
你说得没错，”纳雷瓦轻叹着表示同意，“不过，我们根本无法改变过去，即便是像我这样的人也不例外。无休止地猜测原本可能会发生什么，根本无法让我们取得任何进展，亲爱的客人。我宁愿不去纠结那些其实只是变相指责的‘如果当时……会怎样’之类的问题。”

哼……你在这里白白浪费了时间，而且很可能还让情况变得更糟。在指责别人的时候，你真的应该坚持使用客观事实才对。

rows.translation: 它们本可以做得更好才对！
rows.raw: '"They could have been much better, too!"'

rows.original: "Consider it this way," Nareva continues. "Phyria, you should have known through your mother that Tychris had quite the standing army, even if it was then largely comprised of mercenaries. Of course, after losing you, she was in no mind to do any actual commanding immediately after — no matter how you remember her, she loved you very much." Ria scoffs. "Now I know you're a lying snake." "Oh, really. She drove you so hard because her eyes were one of the few that could see the rot that was seeping out from Belhar and creeping into the Marches. The opulence, the comfort, the hedonism, she worried it would turn you soft... and resenting constantly being forbidden to do everything remotely fun, you ran straight into the arms of your half-brother." "She was a stick in the mud." Phyria's words are ever so slightly more subdued than it was a moment ago. "Perhaps. But she meant well, and like it or not, what your mother put you through hardened you into the fine young woman you are." "I still don't believe you."
rows.translation: 这样想吧，”纳雷瓦继续说道，“菲莉亚，你本应该通过你母亲了解到，提克里斯其实拥有一支相当规模的常备军，尽管当时那支军队主要由雇佣兵组成。当然，在失去了你之后，她短期内根本没心思去指挥军队——无论你如何回忆她，她其实非常爱你。” 莉亚嗤之以鼻。现在 我知道你就是一条会撒谎的蛇。” “哦，是吗？她之所以对你如此严厉，是因为她才是为数不多能够看到贝尔哈尔内部正在蔓延的腐朽势力，以及这些势力是如何逐渐侵蚀边境地区的人。那些奢华的生活、舒适的环境、享乐主义……她担心这些会让你变得软弱。……而且因为总是被禁止做那些看似有趣的事情而心怀怨恨，你最终投入了你同父异母的兄弟的怀抱。” “她真是个固执的人。”菲莉亚的语气比刚才稍微缓和了一些。 也许吧。但她出发点是好的，不管你愿不愿意承认，你母亲让你经历的一切，确实把你锻炼成了如今这个优秀的年轻女性。” “我还是不相信你。

rows.original: "Naturally, my dear guest." Nareva replies, an impish grin on her face. "Well then, Phyria. I am the goddess of secrets, and your mother and I spent many a night over a game of chess or discussing her next offensive against the wraiths. Tell me, which of your embarrassing secrets would you have me spill to prove my words?" Ria says nothing, but stands her ground as her fists curl into balls, her tail twitching agitatedly. "I believe that's the metric we're going by, right? For me to say something only the two of you would have known? Or perhaps would you have preferred some minute mannerism of hers that I could only have observed by being in her presence? Ah, I know! This one will be good." At that, the serpentine goddess cups a hand to her mouth, as if to whisper. Ria stiffens, responding to a voice only she can hear, and at length her cheeks color and her shoulders slump in defeat. "There's no way... Mom and I..." "She swore to take it to the grave, yes, but since she believed you dead — and not wrongly so — there was little need to keep that particular little secret. I remember it clearly: the prince's strategos and a goddess, discussing the foibles of young children over mulled wine... Phyria, no matter how little you think of your own mother, it is always hard for a parent to outlive their child." "Then let Ander and I go so we can finally be with them." Nareva taps her chin theaterically, pretending to consider the matter. "Hmm... I would, I suppose, but [pc.name] here has yet to convince me that I've acted beyond my purview. Still, I hope I've demonstrated sufficiently what Tychris — both city and lineage alike — mean to me. I've grown quite fond of you all in these last couple centuries, and your parents have given me some very good memories. I still remember them as if they had happened yesterday..." As Nareva and Ria go off on a tangent, you listen in on all the details the former dredges up. Advisor, strategist, socialite, confidante... it seems like Nareva played all these parts to the house of Tychris, and remembers her time with them in great detail. That might serve as a clue...
rows.translation: 当然可以，我亲爱的客人。”娜雷瓦脸上带着调皮的笑容回答道，“那么，菲莉亚，我…… 是 秘密的女神啊，我和你母亲曾经有许多个夜晚一起下棋，或者讨论她接下来该如何对付那些幽灵。告诉我，你那些令人尴尬的秘密中，哪一条你愿意让我透露出来，来证明我的话是真的呢？ 莉亚没有说话，只是紧紧地站在那里，双拳紧紧握成拳头，尾巴也焦躁地抽动着。 我想，这才是我们评判的标准吧？如果我说出一些只有你们两个人才知道的事情，会不会不太合适呢？或者，或许你们更希望我提到她某些只有在她面前才能观察到的细微习惯吧？啊，我想我知道了！这个答案应该会很不错。 就在这时，那位蛇形女神将一只手放在嘴边，仿佛在低语着什么。莉亚的身体突然僵硬起来，因为她听到了只有自己才能听到的声音。最终，她的脸颊泛起了红晕，肩膀也无力地垂了下来。 “不可能。我和妈妈……” “她曾发誓要把这个秘密带进坟墓，没错。但既然她以为你已经死了——而她的判断并没有错——那么这个秘密也就没什么必要继续保密了。我记得很清楚：王子的谋士们和一位女神一起，边喝着热酒边讨论着小孩子们的那些愚蠢行为。.. 菲莉亚，无论你对自己母亲的感情有多淡漠，对于父母来说，活过自己的孩子总是件非常艰难的事。 那就让安德和我去吧，这样我们终于可以和他们在一起了。” 纳雷瓦故作思考地摸了摸下巴，说道：“嗯……我想也是，不过…… [pc.name] 这些还远远不足以让我相信我的行为超出了我的职责范围。不过，我希望我已经充分表达了Tychris——无论是这座城市还是它的传承——对我而言意味着什么。在过去的几个世纪里，我越来越喜欢你们所有人了，而你们的父母也给我留下了许多美好的回忆。 我仍然记得那些事情，就好像它们发生在昨天一样…… 当纳雷瓦和莉亚开始聊些不相干的事情时，你仔细聆听了她所讲述的那些细节。顾问、战略家、社交名流、知己……看来纳雷瓦在提克里斯家族中扮演了所有这些角色，而且她对自己与他们共度的那些时光记忆得非常清晰。 这或许能提供一个线索……

rows.original: "It should be easy enough to prove to Ria you knew her mother."
rows.translation: 向莉亚证明你认识她母亲应该并不难吧。
rows.raw: '"It should be easy enough to prove to Ria you knew her mother."'

rows.original:
"Truth is often stranger than fiction, my dear [pc.name], for the simple reason it has no need of verisimilitude. Ander here knows that better than most, doesn't he?"

        Ander winces, but says nothing. 
        
        "Nevertheless, whether you believe me or not doesn't matter. An appeal to incredulity, as they say, is not an argument. Some of the secrets I'm currently caretaking would be quite impossible to believe, I assure you. You should really try harder next time."
        
        Damn, she's got you. There goes your mouth, getting ahead of your mind again... again, baseless accusations aren't going to help you in the slightest, not when dealing with her. Maybe you ought to start from the top and try again...
rows.translation:
亲爱的，事实往往比虚构的故事更加离奇。 [pc.name]原因很简单，它根本不需要具备真实性。安德在这里比大多数人都更清楚这一点，不是吗？”

安德微微皱了皱眉，但什么也没说。

“不过，无论你信不信我，这其实都无关紧要。 正如人们所说，这种试图激发人们怀疑的态度其实并不算是一种有效的论证。我目前负责守护的一些秘密，确实让人难以置信，我可以向你保证。下次你真的应该更加努力一些才行。

该死，她真的把你骗到了。 又说话太急了，又先入为主了……再说一次，毫无根据的指责对你毫无帮助，尤其是在处理她的事情时。也许你应该从头开始，再试一次……

rows.original: "I find it quite hard to believe myself."
rows.translation: 我实在很难相信自己真的做到了这一点。
rows.raw: '"I find it quite hard to believe myself."'

rows.original:
For several moments, Ria and Nareva stare at each other; you can feel the air between them chill. Eventually, the serpentine goddess smiles and shrugs lazily.

        "We all appear to have fallen silent. Is this the end of the conversation, then?"
        
        "No, not quite yet," you reply. "I just wanted to... ah, give the both of you some space."
        
        "Trust me, we have plenty of space between us," Nareva says with a sigh. "Come now, let's finish this posthaste, shall we?"
rows.translation:
有那么几秒钟，莉亚和娜雷瓦彼此对视着，空气中仿佛弥漫着寒意。最终，这位身形如蛇的女神懒洋洋地笑了笑，耸了耸肩。

“看来我们都沉默不语了……那么，这次谈话就到此结束了吗？”

“不，并没有结束。”你回答道，“我只是想……嗯，给你们俩一些空间。”

“相信我，我们之间已经有足够的空间了。”娜雷瓦叹了口气说道，“好了，我们赶紧把这件事解决掉吧。

rows.original:
"So he is, my dear [pc.name]. Or more correctly, was; I'm sure the current Lord and Lady en Tychris would have problems recognising him as such. But alas, he is in a realm where his title and lineage have but only sentimental value, a currency which he is currently frittering away at an alarming rate. If I were in his position, I would be more careful about losing such goodwill; while I'm not the kind of goddess who demands bowing and scraping, I do expect one to be able to control one's passions.

        "Now then, where were we...?"
rows.translation:
是啊，亲爱的。 [pc.name]或者更准确地说，曾经是；我敢肯定，现在的恩·提克里斯勋爵和夫人肯定认不出他来了。但可惜的是，他现在所处的这个地方，他的头衔和血统只不过具有象征意义而已，而这些“象征意义”正在以惊人的速度被他浪费掉。如果我处在他的位置，我会更加小心，不会轻易失去这些“好感”；虽然我不是那种要求别人卑躬屈膝的女神，但我确实期望人们能够控制自己的情绪。

“那么，我们刚才说到哪里了……？

rows.original:
"Well, he is being held against his will, so that's technically correct. Of course, it says nothing of whether I'm entirely within my rights to detain him as I please. And if Philander here recognizes his situation... then he ought to be behaving better. Given my fondness for his parents, I don't want to have to reprimand either him or his sister, but I will not tolerate tomfoolery by others in my domain — a sentiment Philander himself should be well familiar with, yes? I would hate for this to turn... unpleasant."

        Philander begins to scowl, then catches himself and stifles it.
        
        "Good. Now, where were we before we got sidetracked?"
rows.translation:
嗯，他确实是被强行关押着的，从这个意义上来说，这种说法是正确的。当然，这并不能说明我是否有完全的权利按照自己的意愿将他关押起来。而如果这里的菲兰德能够认识到自己的处境……那么他就应该表现得更好一些。 鉴于我对他父母的喜爱，我确实不希望不得不责备他或他的妹妹，但我绝不能容忍别人在我的地盘上胡闹——这一点，菲兰德本人应该很清楚才对，不是吗？我可不想让这件事发展成不好的局面。……真不愉快。”

菲兰德开始皱起眉头，但很快又克制住了自己。

“好了。那么，在我们被这些事情打断之前，我们到底在讨论什么来着？

rows.original: You hold your tongue and let the tension pass. Thankfully, unlike his half-sister, Ander is more inclined to swallow his pride. "Thank you. I don't mean to intimidate, but I'd like to remind you that you are in my domain, and completely and utterly within my power. You wouldn't like it if guests started arguing with you in your own home, would you?" "Suppose not," Ander mumbles resentfully. "Indeed, I can cut this conversation off any time I like." "Yes, the conversation," you say. "Speaking of which, I was asking you if you knew any details regarding what happened to Ander and Ria. If you were around to whisk their souls into your Dream, you must've been nearby, right?" Nareva looks thoughtful and taps her chin. "Hmm... it's been a while since then. Years and decades are one thing, centuries another. Memories grow distant, and lose clarity..." Ria looks aghast. "You're saying that you don't remember!?" "It's a concept the both of you should be familiar with, really. Though larger than yours, my working memory is still not infinite, which is why I have to rely on records to keep track of knowledge. Records, say, like your beloved brother here, or my Well. If you don't mind waiting for me to do a thorough search for every last detail I can scrape together..." [var0 |Something sounds suspicious here. Perhaps it's time to use that clue... |"There's clearly no time for that!" A shrug. "Oh well, what a pity. My word against yours, is it, Phyria?" rows.raw: ' You hold your tongue and let the tension pass. Thankfully, unlike his half-sister, Ander is more inclined to swallow his pride. "Thank you. I don't mean to intimidate, but I'd like to remind you that you are in my domain, and completely and utterly within my power. You wouldn't like it if guests started arguing with you in your own home, would you?" "Suppose not," Ander mumbles resentfully. "Indeed, I can cut this conversation off any time I like." "Yes, the conversation," you say. "Speaking of which, I was asking you if you knew any details regarding what happened to Ander and Ria. If you were around to whisk their souls into your Dream, you must've been nearby, right?" Nareva looks thoughtful and taps her chin. "Hmm... it's been a while since then. Years and decades are one thing, centuries another. Memories grow distant, and lose clarity..." Ria looks aghast. "You're saying that you don't remember!?" "It's a concept the both of you should be familiar with, really. Though larger than yours, my working memory is still not infinite, which is why I have to rely on records to keep track of knowledge. Records, say, like your beloved brother here, or my Well. If you don't mind waiting for me to do a thorough search for every last detail I can scrape together..." [var0 |Something sounds suspicious here. Perhaps it's time to use that clue... |"There's clearly no time for that!" A shrug. "Oh well, what a pity. My word against yours, is it, Phyria?" "...Clever. Verrry clever. I can see why everyone's so interested in you, [pc.race]."

            You grin. "I've no doubt your love for the en Tychris line is genuine, goddess. All the intimate moments you were recounting to Ria with crystal clarity... and yet for some strange reason, you can't seem to recall the details of a terrible tragedy that took the life of both the heir and the spare."
            
            "Ah, well. Like you said, it was such a terrible tragedy... these things do bring with them desires to forget. We are more alike you than you might imagine us to be...I'm sure you've experienced your own desires to put unpalatable memories out of mind? Pity, and our conversation was going so smoothly, too."
rows.translation: ……真聪明。聪明极了。现在我明白为什么大家都对你这么感兴趣了。 [pc.race]你笑了。“女神，我毫不怀疑你对恩·提克里斯家族的热爱是真挚的。你向莉亚讲述的那些亲密时刻，每一个细节都如此清晰……然而，出于某种奇怪的原因，你似乎却记不起那场夺去了继承人及备选继承人生命的悲剧的详细经过。啊，好吧。正如你所说，那确实是一场极其可怕的悲剧……这样的经历确实会让人产生想要遗忘的欲望。其实，我们之间的相似之处比你想象的要多……我相信你也曾经有过想要将那些令人不快的回忆从脑海中抹去的冲动吧？ 真遗憾，我们的谈话本来进行得这么顺利啊。

rows.original:
"Yes, yes, horrific indeed," Nareva replies, looking thoughtful. "All of Philander's students, the servants he'd dragged out from Tychris to cater the event, everyone — save Sigrune, that is — all consumed like helpless sheep. A shame. In all of my existence, I'd scarcely seen such outright butchery. It makes one want to put the uglier details out of one's mind for the sake of one's sanity."

        "And that's why you deliberately set this event out of your mind?"
        
        "Just so. I can always consult the Well should I have need to."
        
        Grr... you know Nareva's being wilfully obtuse here, but you can't prove anything. While pressing her without a valid point isn't the smartest idea, she isn't going to run her mouth without some encouragement. Maybe you should've considered that...

“所以，这就是你故意选择忘记这件事的原因吗？只是为了方便以后需要时可以随时查阅资料而已。”

rows.original:
Nareva raises an eyebrow. "Yes, what about that?"

        "It's just that particular turn of phrase, that our conversation was going so smoothly... what a strange way of putting things. It almost sounds as if you deliberately didn't want it to take this turn... is it that you don't want to discuss what happened to the siblings that day?"
        
        "Come now, my dear guest. Clearly you're just overthinking this — reading so much into a simple turn of phrase? Really?"
        
        "It's not just a turn of phrase. You've been surprisingly evasive whenever the topic of the siblings' demise comes up. That, and you lied about not being able to remember the day at all. I should've suspected something, considering how well you've reproduced the convocation in this Dream of yours."
        
        "Ah... these are merely Philander's recollections of the event, plucked from his mind to give him the most comfort while he's been here with me. A delightfully hedonistic cornucopia to-be of gluttony, prurience, inebriation... and learning, of course. Compared to the scene of gore and horror, his servants and students reduced to empty husks... well, that's not the sort of memory one wants to live with, right? A good thing he felt nothing when his body was destroyed."
        
        You shake your head. "Goddess or not, after all this I simply can't bring myself to believe that you've allowed the details to slip your mind. Not after everything you've said; it sounds like you've had the goal of avoiding this topic from the outset."
        
        Nareva recoils, feigning shock. "Oh my, oh my. You make me sound almost crooked. And to think I've always had the best of intentions..."
rows.translation:
纳雷瓦挑了挑眉毛：“嗯，那又怎么样？”

“就是那个表达方式……我们的谈话本来进行得如此顺利……用那种方式来说，未免太奇怪了。听起来你似乎是故意不想让谈话朝那个方向发展……难道你是不想谈论那天那对兄妹发生了什么吗？
        
        来吧，我亲爱的客人。显然你只是想得太多了——把一个简单的措辞解读得如此复杂？真的吗？”

“这不仅仅是一个措辞的问题。每当提到兄弟姐妹的死亡这件事时，你的反应总是出奇地回避。还有，你谎称自己完全想不起那一天的细节。考虑到你在你的这个梦境中把那次聚会描述得如此逼真，我本应该怀疑一些什么的。
        
        啊……这些只不过是菲兰德对那段经历的回忆，是他为了在和我在一起的日子里获得些许慰藉而回想出来的。这些回忆充满了享乐主义的气息，充满了暴食、淫欲、醉酒……当然，也包含着学习。与那些血腥恐怖的场景相比，他的仆人和学生们都变成了空壳……嗯，这样的回忆，谁也不想一直铭记在心吧？幸好，当他的身体被毁掉的时候，他并没有感到任何痛苦。
        
        你摇了摇头。“无论你是不是女神，经历了这一切之后，我真的无法相信你会忘记这些细节。毕竟你说了那么多话，听起来从一开始你就刻意回避这个话题。
        
        纳雷瓦故作震惊，连连后退：“天哪，天哪。你这么说，让我听起来好像是个坏人一样。而我本来可是怀着最好的意图啊……

"It looks like you've fallen silent," Nareva says after an awkward pause. "Are we done here, then?"

        "No! I just need some time to... ah, collect my thoughts," you reply.
        
        "If you say so, if you say so. Do remember that I'm the goddess of secrets; I'm not one so inclined to speak my mind. If you wanted someone who can natter on for hours unprompted, why don't I introduce you to Lumia or Sorra? They'd be happy to accommodate your silence."
        
        "...Maybe another time."

“……也许下次吧。

rows.original: "Oh, simply ask anyone in Tychris the things I have done ever since I formally became their patron goddess. For more than two hundred years now, I have done nothing but good, starting with the preservation of their city state against the scourging tides of darkness that swept away old Belhar and much of the world beyond. In fact, I would argue that the only reason it stands today is because of my direct intervention. Phyria's mother was an impressive woman, but she was by no means representative of the general citizenry." "I don't believe — " "What you believe or don't believe is immaterial here, as are any imaginary motives you choose to assign me. What the facts have borne out is that I have only done good by the en Tychris line ever since they accepted me, and nothing you say will change that."
rows.translation: 哦，只要向提克里斯的任何人询问一下，自从我正式成为他们的守护女神以来，我做了哪些事情就行了。两百多年来，我所做的每一件事都是好事——从保护他们的城邦，使其免受那些吞噬了古老的贝哈尔以及世界上许多其他地区的黑暗势力的侵袭开始，我就一直在做有益于人们的事情。 事实上，我认为它能够延续至今，唯一的原因就是我的直接干预。菲莉亚的母亲确实是一位了不起的女性，但她绝不能代表普通民众的整体状况。 “我并不相信—— 你相信什么或不相信什么在这里并不重要，你也完全可以随意给我安上一些想象中的动机。重要的是…… 事实 事实已经证明，自从他们接纳我以来，我做的一切都是好事，你说什么都无法改变这一点。

rows.original:
"Hmm..."

        You shrug and smirk up at Nareva's serpentine coils. "If you wish to clear your name, goddess, then simply speak plainly and don't play dumb when confronted with topics you don't want to speak of."
        
        A beatific smile. "Memory is a fickle thing, my dear [pc.race]. Look, allow me to illustrate my point — Ander here was the star of the show, and even he doesn't recall everything about it. Now, Philander, do you recall everyone whom you invited to attend your convocation?"
        
        Ander frowns. "Most, but not all. Father insisted that I have over a number of personages I didn't really care for... since I knew they were going to be there out of politeness and not out of any interest in mirror magic, they were all the same to me."
        
        "And do you know the expense at which your convocation was held?"
        
        "That I never knew in the first place, since I handled none of the logistics for the event," Ander replies, shaking his head. "I was too busy with preparing the material I intended to impart to my students... Ria was tasked with security and managing Sigrune. The numbers were boring, so I left everything to our lord steward and that was that. Not that we got to taste any of it in the end... the refreshments were scheduled to start in the intermission after my first series of lectures, but before I got to the meat of the matter."
        
        "Indeed, none of them ever woke up and got to sample the braised duck or chilled port paid for with the taxes of his people, or any other manner of expensive delicacies lugged all the way from the heartlands and served up on that same fine glassware Tychris is so famous for. It's such a pity, especially considering the cost of the convocation put quite a sizeable dent in what funding was available for the first skirmishes of the Godswar." 
        
        Ander gulps. Ria glowers.
        
        "In any case," Nareva continues, "Have I demonstrated the fallibility of one's memory? It is, after all, why we put our thoughts down to paper, where they do not decay as easily, or in my case, consign them to the Well. That is, unless you're going to find fault with the prince's statements?"
rows.translation:
嗯……”

你耸了耸肩，对着纳雷瓦那蜿蜒盘旋的形态露出一丝 smirk：“如果女神您真的想洗清自己的名声，那就直说吧。遇到那些您不想谈论的话题时，就别装傻了。”

她露出了一抹安详的微笑：“记忆这种东西啊，实在是很不可靠，亲爱的。 [pc.race]听着，让我来说明一下我的意思——安德才是这场活动的主角，就连他也不记得所有的事情了。现在，菲兰德，你还记得你邀请了哪些人参加你的聚会吗？”

安德皱起了眉头：“大部分人都记得，但不是全部。父亲坚持让我邀请了一些我其实并不感兴趣的人……因为我知道他们参加只是出于礼貌，并非对镜像魔法真的感兴趣，所以对他们来说，这些人其实都是一样的。
        
        那么，你知道这次会议的花费是多少吗？”

“我一开始就根本不知道，因为这次活动的后勤工作根本不是我负责的，”安德尔摇着头回答，“我当时一直在忙于准备那些打算传授给学生的资料。.. 蕾亚被负责安保工作以及管理西格鲁娜的事宜。那些数字报表实在枯燥无味，所以我把所有工作都交给了我们的管家，就这样罢了。不过最后我们也没机会品尝到那些准备好的点心……那些点心本应在我的第一系列讲座休息期间供应，但在我开始讲解主要内容之前，这些安排就被取消了。"
        
        事实上，他们中没有一个人有机会品尝到那些用他的子民缴纳的税款购买的炖鸭或冰镇波特酒，也没有人能够享受到那些从内陆地区运来、用提克里斯那闻名的精美玻璃器皿盛装的昂贵美食。实在是一件遗憾的事，尤其是考虑到这次召集会议所花费的资金，已经大大削减了用于发动‘神战’初期战役的经费。 
        
        安德咽了口唾沫，莉亚则怒目而视。

“无论如何，”纳雷瓦继续说道，“我是否已经证明了人类记忆的可靠性是有限的？毕竟，这就是我们把想法记录下来的原因——这样它们就不会那么容易被遗忘。至于我，我会把它们保存在‘井’里。当然，除非你们打算对王子的陈述提出异议……

        "If you say so, if you say so. Do remember that I'm the goddess of secrets; I'm not one so inclined to speak my mind. If you wanted someone who can natter on for hours unprompted, why don't I introduce you to Lumia or Sorra? They'd be happy to accommodate your silence."
        
        "...Maybe another time."

看起来你沉默不语了，”在一段尴尬的沉默之后，纳雷瓦说道，“那么，我们在这里谈的事情就结束了吗？”

“不！我只是需要一些时间来……嗯，整理一下思路。”你回答道。

“……也许下次吧。

rows.original: "Come on," you say to Ander. "Try to remember. We can't lose to her like this!" The prince frowns, closes his eyes, and rubs his temples. After a while, he shakes his head and curls his tail about himself. "I'm sorry, [pc.name]. I really don't recall." Urk! "I had Mother prepare the invitations from Father's guest list — she was so much more eloquent than me — then signed and sealed them posthaste. I know I looked over each one to make sure no one I really didn't want there was going to be attending, but I don't remember everyone whom I invited to the convocation. My friends, yes, but the rest..." Ander gives you a rueful smile. "I was just so excited, I didn't care about such mundane things." Nareva beams. "See? Even the prince agrees." Even so... there must be a way out of this. You have to find it, Ander and Ria are depending on you!
rows.translation: 加油，”你对安德说，“努力回想一下吧。我们不能就这样输给她！” 王子皱起了眉头，闭上眼睛，揉了揉太阳穴。过了一会儿，他摇了摇头，把尾巴卷在身上：“对不起…… [pc.name]我真的想不起来了。” “哎呀！” “我让妈妈根据爸爸准备的宾客名单去准备邀请函——她说话可比我圆滑多了——然后我赶紧签好名字并盖了章。我记得我仔细检查了每一份邀请函，以确保没有遗漏任何应该邀请的人…… 真的 我本来不希望会有人不来参加，但我实在想不起自己邀请了哪些人来参加这次聚会。我的朋友们肯定会来，但其他人……”安德露出无奈的笑容，“当时我实在太兴奋了，根本没考虑这些琐事。” 纳雷瓦高兴地笑道：“看吧？就连王子也同意了。” 不过……肯定还有解决办法的。你必须找到它，安德和莉亚都在指望你呢！

rows.original: Yes... yes. There's definitely something wrong with what Nareva just said. Again, she claims to have a spotty memory of the events, yet knows things that even Ander doesn't. There's no doubt about it, she had to be there at the moment it all happened. How else would she have known rather insignificant details like the refreshments being served, or even the dishes they were served on? You've got her now, and with the same mistake twice in a row! "...!" "A poor memory isn't rather befitting of a goddess of knowledge, is it? In your haste to use Ander to defend yourself, you didn't think he'd say a little too much." "The prince's memories..." "...Should have no recollection of the refreshments, and neither should Ria's; they died before they were ever served. If this dream realm is recreated through the siblings' memories, no wonder there's no food or drink on display. What was it Ander said to me when I met him? 'Otherwise we could all just leave before the orgies and drinking even gets started'? "For a goddess, you're a rather poor liar. Clearly you're not used to it — is there something you're looking to hide? Something to do with how the siblings perished?" For the first time since she came on the scene, Nareva's smug, self-satisfied air dissipates as she turns her lips in a scowl. "I... am not at liberty to disclose that." That denial's as good as a confession. "Then you do recall the events of that day?" A sigh. "Yes, I do. A warning, and I do not mean this as a threat: if you continue down this road, [pc.race], you may not like what you discover." Well, if that doesn't sound ominous. "I'll see about that. All I want is Ander and Ria to be free." "And I cannot release them. After all this... you still haven't taken apart my premises." [pc.cunningRange 60 |No, but you wager that the reason she's keeping Ander and Ria here has something to do with why she doesn't want to speak about the circumstances of their death. The two must be related, and if you can get at that truth...! ] "Not yet... but if that's what it takes." "Then it seems our game must continue to its bitter end."

rows.translation: 物流方面似乎存在一些问题。

rows.original:
Nareva smiles again; that smug attitude is really starting to grate, even if she has every right to be. "Well? You have no rebuttal here, do you?"

        "I do, I just need to find a way to prise this situation open."
        
        "Ah, the optimism and tenacity of you mortals. It's one of the things I love about you, even if it can be irritating at times. Like I said, we have time."
rows.translation:
纳雷瓦又笑了；那种自鸣得意的态度真的开始让人感到烦躁了，尽管她确实有这样的理由。“怎么样？你没有什么反驳的理由了吧？”

“我有的，只是需要想办法打破这种僵局而已。”

“啊，人类们的这种乐观和坚韧精神，正是我喜欢你们的地方之一，尽管有时候也会让人感到恼火。就像我之前说的，我们还有时间。

rows.original: Since you've come this far... perhaps it's time to re-analyze the state of the battle. Nareva is no longer feigning ignorance of the day when the royal siblings died, yet that merely opens up a thousand more questions that you'd like to ask her. Furthermore, she's right in that you haven't taken apart her stated reason for keeping Ander and Ria as prisoners in this dream world of hers. However, it's clear that the goddess is hiding something that's related to that fateful day, something she really doesn't want to bring up... and you have the distinct feeling that if you can get at the truth of what happened, it'll at least shed some light on the true reason they're being kept here. "So," you say. "Tell us the details of how the Convocation of Mirrors met its grisly end." Nareva nods. "The Prince relied on the plateau's steep bluffs to keep unwanted guests away from the convocation, expecting no more resistance than a harpy or two; the handful of royal guards Ria had brought along with her would have been able to handle most flying threats. With Sigrune guarding the tunnel that led up to the convocation grounds, they felt safe enough. Alas, heights were no impediment to the largely immaterial wraiths, who descended upon the mages as they slept. "Philander, your father was right: large concentrations of magic don't just attract demons, but any manner of beings which derive sustenance from it... or its practitioners, for that matter. It's a small mercy that your father refused to let you hold the convocation in the palace — imagine what would have happened if your first contact with the wraiths had been in your own home instead." "With far more men and resources at our side, we could've had a chance of fighting these creatures off," Ria points out. "Perhaps, perhaps. You have your mother's blood, Phyria, and your personal command was certainly a cut above even the royal guard. Then again, with the opulence of the House of Tychris such that even the servants and hirelings were able to indulge in the pleasures and pleasantries, I'm not sure that's too high a bar to clear. "Either way, those still awake were granted one small mercy: with the prince and his students the most tantalising dishes on display, the wraiths went straight for them and ignored the lesser morsels running and screaming about the grounds. Some of the servants attempted to hide, a futile endeavor since wraiths do not see the world as you do. Others threw themselves off the plateau in a desperate hope; a few managed to make it into the tunnels leading back to the forest, but since Sigrune continued to stand guard for more than two centuries, it's safe to assume none of them ever emerged safely. "The royal guard did what they could, but weapons of steel were little proof against the wraiths' ethereal natures. Eventually, they too broke ranks and fled — to none of their shame, considering what they were up against." Ander ponders this, his mouth set into a grim, straight line. "So... distasteful as it must be, I must ask how these wraiths fed, as you put it. I'm sure you understand that as a scholar, I must know." "Of course," Nareva replies. "First, the monsters consume the victim's spiritual energy, as what the magic practitioners of [pc.name]'s day would call it. The soul, in addition to one's thoughts, emotions and memories. This leaves the victim little more than a suggestible shell, a meat puppet to be directed by the wraith should it need a servant. If the wraith in question has no need of servants, well, even physical energy is consumed, leaving anything from a lifeless husk to a small pile of ashen dust as the remnants of one's meal. Much akin to how some people will leave the bones, while others will crack them to get at the marrow." "And you came in the midst of all this?" you say. "That's correct. The siblings' bodies lay at the center of the convocation, ringed by Ander's students... the bulk of the wraiths had yet to get to them. Their souls had been gnawed at, but not devoured — injured, but not killed. Being of royal blood and trained, they were made of sterner stuff than the others present, and I was able to spirit them away to safety while the convocation was torn apart at the seams. "That is the truth of the day. Having absorbed the memories, personalities and souls of almost all who were present atop the plateau, Tychris was their next destination, poor, bereaved Tychris. Since then, Ander and Ria have been here with me in my Dream, waiting for someone worthy to come along and receive the secret of mirror magic. That's the least I can do for Ander, realize his dream even in death. Do you understand now?" You're beginning to understand, yes, but as before, you're certain the goddess is hiding something. Deity or not, you're going to wring it out of her and see the siblings free!
rows.translation: 既然你已经走到这一步了……或许现在是时候重新审视这场战斗的现状了。纳雷瓦已经不再假装对王室兄弟姐妹遇害的那天一无所知，但这样一来，反而引出了更多你想问她的问题。 此外，她说得对——你确实没有仔细分析过她之所以要把安德和莉亚囚禁在这个幻想世界里的原因。 然而，很明显，这位女神在隐瞒一些与那个决定性的日子有关的真相，一些她实在不愿意提及的事情。.. 你有一种强烈的感觉，那就是只要能够弄清楚究竟发生了什么，至少就能弄清楚他们被关在这里的真正原因。 “那么，”你说道，“请告诉我们‘镜之集会’是如何走向悲剧结局的吧。纳雷瓦点了点头。 王子依靠高原上陡峭的悬崖来阻挡那些不速之客，他预计遇到的抗性最多也就是一两只女妖而已；瑞亚带来的那几名皇家卫兵也足以应对大多数飞行中的威胁。既然西格鲁娜负责守卫通往会议场地的隧道，他们就觉得足够安全了。然而，对于那些几乎毫无实体的幽灵来说，高度根本不是障碍——它们在法师们熟睡时降临到了他们身上。 菲兰德，你父亲说得对：高浓度的魔法不仅会吸引恶魔，还会吸引任何以魔法为食的生物……当然，那些使用魔法的人也不例外。你父亲没有允许你在宫殿里举行这次集会，也算是件好事——想象一下，如果你是在自己家里第一次遇到那些幽灵，会发生什么。” “如果我们有更多的人手和资源，或许就有机会将这些生物赶走。”莉亚指出。 也许吧，也许吧。菲莉亚，你身上流淌着你母亲的血液，而你的指挥能力确实远超皇家卫队。不过，考虑到提克里斯家族的富庶程度——就连仆从和雇工们也能享受各种奢华与便利，我觉得这个标准其实并不算太高。 无论如何，那些仍然醒着的人还是得到了一点小小的宽慰：由于王子和他的学生们面前摆着那些最诱人的菜肴，那些幽灵们直接扑向了那些食物，而完全忽略了那些在场地里四处奔跑、尖叫的次要目标。 有些仆从试图躲藏起来，但这是徒劳的——因为怨灵看待世界的方式与你不同。另一些人则绝望地从高原上跳了下去；其中有一小部分人成功进入了通往森林的隧道，但由于西格鲁娜在那里守卫了两个多世纪，可以肯定的是，他们中没有一个人能够安全地逃脱。 皇家卫队已经竭尽全力，但钢铁武器对于那些幽灵般的存在来说几乎毫无作用。最终，他们也不得不在恐惧中四散逃亡——考虑到他们所面对的敌人，这种行为丝毫不可耻。安德若有所思地凝视着前方，嘴唇紧抿成一条僵硬的直线。“那么……尽管这一定很令人不快，但我还是必须问一下，你们所说的这些幽灵究竟是如何获取食物的。作为一位学者，我当然有必要了解这些。” “当然，”纳雷瓦回答道。 首先，这些怪物会吸收受害者的精神能量，正如那些魔法师们所描述的那样。 [pc.name]当天到来时，灵魂便会脱离一个人的思想、情感与记忆，使其沦为一个极易被影响的空壳，一个可以被怨灵驱使的肉体傀儡。倘若那怨灵并不需要这样的仆从，那么就连身体所蕴含的能量也会被消耗殆尽，最终那个人就只会剩下一个毫无生气的空壳，或者是一堆灰烬，就像吃完饭后留下的残渣一样。 这就好比有些人会直接留下骨头，而另一些人则会把骨头敲碎才能得到骨髓。” “而你，却出现在这一切发生的时刻？”你问道。 没错。那对兄妹的尸体位于集会场的中央，周围环绕着安德的学生们……大多数怨灵还没有袭击到他们。他们的灵魂确实受到了侵蚀，但并没有被吞噬——他们受了伤，但并没有死亡。由于他们出身王室，又接受了训练，所以他们的体质比在场的其他人都要强韧。因此，当集会场陷入混乱时，我才能够将他们安全地带走。 这就是今天的真相。当提克里斯吸收了几乎所有曾经站在高原上的人的记忆、个性与灵魂之后，它就成了他们的下一个目标——可怜的、失去一切的提克里斯。从那以后，安德和莉亚就一直和我一起，在我的梦境中等待着，等待着一个值得拥有这个秘密的人出现，来继承镜像魔法的奥秘。 这是我为安德能做的最起码的事了，即使在他死后也要帮他实现梦想。现在你明白了吗？” “你开始明白了一些，没错，但和之前一样，你仍然觉得这位女神在隐瞒什么。不管她是不是神明，你都要把她藏起来的秘密弄清楚，让那对兄妹重获自由！

This leaves the victim little more than a suggestible shell, a meat puppet to be directed by the wraith should it need a servant. If the wraith in question has no need of servants, well, even physical energy is consumed, leaving anything from a lifeless husk to a small pile of ashen dust as the remnants of one's meal. Much akin to how some people will leave the bones, while others will crack them to get at the marrow." "And you came in the midst of all this?" you say. "That's correct. The siblings' bodies lay at the center of the convocation, ringed by Ander's students... the bulk of the wraiths had yet to get to them. Their souls had been gnawed at, but not devoured — injured, but not killed. Being of royal blood and trained, they were made of sterner stuff than the others present, and I was able to spirit them away to safety while the convocation was torn apart at the seams. "That is the truth of the day. Having absorbed the memories, personalities and souls of almost all who were present atop the plateau, Tychris was their next destination, poor, bereaved Tychris. Since then, Ander and Ria have been here with me in my Dream, waiting for someone worthy to come along and receive the secret of mirror magic. That's the least I can do for Ander, realize his dream even in death. Do you understand now?" You're beginning to understand, yes, but as before, you're certain the goddess is hiding something. Deity or not, you're going to wring it out of her and see the siblings free!"

rows.original: "Isn't there something else you could've done?" you ask. "Anything but keeping Ander and Ria captive here with you all this time?" Nareva shrugs. "I really don't get why you all have this obsession with oblivion. Philander certainly was excited by the prospect of having stumbled upon the secret of immortality. Are you all really that eager to rush headlong into the void?" "Mother would say that there are fates worse than death," Ria replies with a growl. "I don't know about this idiot here, but being kept by a snake-witch as part of her collection, an exhibit to be gawked at by her visitors — that counts in my book!" "Hm. Well, if interacting with my guests is such a terrible prospect for you, I could help you forget them so you would never know, and hence never be bothered by the prospect. Would that be sufficient?" "That's not my point!" This time, it's Ander who steps in to take hold of his half-sister's shoulder, giving it a firm shake. "Ria, I understand how you feel, but this isn't helping. Like it or not, we're completely at her mercy here and we shouldn't make [pc.name]'s job any harder than it already is." Phew. Thank the gods... less the one right in front of you. Nareva sighs, raising two fingers to her temples and rubbing away. "Tell me then, Philander. Knowing the circumstances, what would you have preferred? A chance to spread your teachings and immortalise yourself that way, affecting the world centuries after the lifeless husk of your body's long crumbled to dust? Or for everything in that brilliant mind of yours to be lost for all eternity for the sake of your pride, rendering all your hard work on mirror magic moot?" Ander mulls over this for a little while, chewing his lip as he thinks. At last, he lets his shoulders sag and tail droop. "I don't like to admit it, Ria, she's right. I've been given a second chance that I've no reason to have. If anything, I ought to be grateful." "Get a grip of yourself, brother! Don't fall for her bafflegarble! I can't believe you're seriously trying to convince yourself this is a good thing!" Nareva tuts. "I really don't understand it. The two of you have been existing as if you were in one of Philander's famed dream orgies, wanting nothing at all; it is an existence which many of the living would do much to attain. Eternal pleasure with every hedonistic fantasy fulfilled, ample time with which to engage one's pursuits... you exist as much as you did in life. That someone is keeping you in check should be nothing new to you; the both of you were always answerable to your royal parents. So where exactly is the problem? Do the bars of your cage only chafe when you can see them, or would you prefer the illusion of freedom?" That provokes the siblings into a shouting match; while the siblings argue, you turn back to the serpentine goddess. "So, this is it, then? There was no other way you could have preserved Ander and Ria from the wraiths?" "Ah... time was limited. The wraiths could have looked up from their feasting any moment and noticed me. Things would've gotten messy then — I thought it most prudent to extract the royal siblings first, save them while I could." [var0 |No time, she says? Perhaps you should use that clue here... |"So there was really nothing you could do." "Given the unfortunate circumstances, no. That's the truth of the matter." Hmm. Something doesn't quite add up about Nareva's words, but you can't quite place your finger on it. Perhaps you should try a different line of questioning first and see if you can't glean out some more information from her words... ]
rows.translation: 难道就没有其他办法了吗？”你问道，“除了把安德和莉亚一直囚禁在这里，与你们所有人在一起之外，难道就没有其他办法了吗？” 纳雷瓦耸了耸肩：“我真的不明白，为什么你们所有人都对‘遗忘’如此着迷。 菲兰德确实对偶然发现了永生的秘密这一事实感到兴奋。“你们真的都这么急切地想要冲进那无底的虚空吗？” “母亲会说，有些命运比死亡还要糟糕。”莉亚低声回答道。 我不知道这个蠢货是怎么想的，但被一个蛇女当作她的收藏品来饲养，这…… 展示 被我的访客们盯着看——在我看来，这已经算是一种困扰了！” “嗯，如果与我的访客们互动对你来说真的那么糟糕的话，我可以帮你把他们忘掉，这样你就永远不会知道这件事，也就永远不会因此而烦恼了。这样够吗？ 这并不是我想表达的意思！ 这次，是安德站出来，握住了他同父异母妹妹的肩膀，用力摇晃了一下。“莉亚，我理解你的感受，但这样做并没有什么帮助。不管我们愿不愿意，我们现在完全处于她的摆布之下，我们不应该这样…… [pc.name]让他的工作变得更困难些，真的有这个必要吗？” 呼……谢天谢地……至少不用麻烦眼前这个家伙了。 纳雷瓦叹了口气，用两根手指按住太阳穴，轻轻揉了揉。“那么，菲兰德，你倒是说说看吧。 考虑到这些情况，你会选择什么？是抓住机会传播自己的理念，让自己的名字永垂不朽，让这些理念在数个世纪后依然影响着世界，即使你的躯体早已化为尘土？还是为了维护自己的骄傲，让那颗充满智慧的头脑中的所有知识永远消失，让你在镜像魔法领域所付出的一切努力都付诸东流？安德尔思考了片刻，一边思考一边咬着嘴唇。最终，他耸了耸肩，垂下了尾巴：“我不想承认，莉亚，但她说得对。我得到了一个本不该属于我的第二次机会。 如果说有什么的话，我反而应该感到感激才对。” “冷静点，兄弟！别被她那些花言巧语给骗了！我实在无法相信…… 相信 你真的是在努力让自己相信这是真的吗？ 不错 真是搞不懂！”纳雷瓦嘟囔道，“你们俩过得简直就像在菲兰德那些著名的梦中之宴里一样，什么都不追求；这种生活方式，很多活着的人都会拼命想要拥有的啊。 每当那些享乐主义的幻想得以实现时，你便会感受到永恒的愉悦，也有充足的时间去追求自己感兴趣的事物……你的存在，与在世时一样真实。有人一直在约束你，这一点对你来说应该并不陌生；你们两人一直以来都必须向你们的王室父母负责。 那么，问题究竟出在什么地方呢？是不是只有当你看到那些“笼子的栏杆”时，它们才会让你感到不适，还是说你其实更希望拥有那种自由的感觉呢？ 这一番话引发了兄弟姐妹们的激烈争论；在他们争吵的时候，你则转身走向那位蛇形女神。 所以，真的没有其他办法可以保护安德和莉亚免受那些幽灵的伤害了吗？” “啊……时间太有限了。那些幽灵随时都可能从它们的进食中停下来，注意到我的存在。 那样的话情况就会变得很复杂了——我认为，最明智的做法就是先把王室兄弟姐妹救出来，尽可能地保护他们的安全。 [var0 |没时间，她是这么说的吗？或许你该…… 利用这里的线索吧。... |所以，你真的无能为力。” “在这种不幸的情况下，确实无能为力。事实就是如此。” 嗯，纳雷瓦的话似乎有些地方不太对劲，但你又说不出具体哪里不对。或许你应该再仔细想想。 先尝试换一种提问方式吧。 试着从她的话中挖掘出更多信息吧…… ]

rows.original:
"As unfortunate as it may be, I'm finding fault after fault in your arguments," you say. "Didn't you just claim that wraiths enter quite the stupor after such a heavy feeding? Wasn't that why you said you could enter and walk amidst the convocation unmolested?"

            "Hmm..."
            
            "Keeping track of lies becomes increasingly hard as one is forced to keep doing so in order to cover up previous falsehoods. Maybe if you wish to keep the upper hand here, it would be best to come clean and tell us the truth. It's much easier."
            
            Nareva cups her chin in her hands. "You really are serious. Your refusal to give up is so touching, you know? Philander and Phyria deserve so much less, considering how much they've lived their lives for themselves, instead of for the benefit of others. However, I don't think it's going to do you any good..."
            
            "Why, are you going to give up the reasonable deity schtick after all? Is this where the lightning bolts come in, or will it be the fire and brimstone?"
            
            "No, my dear guest. I'm simply choosing to remind you that you still haven't taken down my premises: that I'm fully in my right to keep the royal siblings here, as per what my portfolio as a deity demands. Very well, allow me to reiterate: I am the goddess of secrets, of knowledge, and of magic. I have, in secret, preserved the knowledge of a unique form of magic. Do you deny this?"
rows.translation:
尽管这很令人遗憾，但我实在是在你的论点中找出了一个又一个漏洞，”你说。“你不是刚刚说过，那些幽灵在进食过量之后会陷入一种昏沉的状态吗？正因为如此，你才声称自己可以毫无阻碍地进入那个集会场所，而在其中自由行动，对吧？

            嗯……”

“当一个人不得不不断编造谎言来掩盖之前的虚假陈述时，跟踪这些谎言就会变得越来越困难。或许，如果你想在这场游戏中占据上风，最好的办法就是坦白相待，告诉我们真相。这样会容易得多。
            
            纳雷瓦双手部托着下巴说道：“你真的是认真的啊。你这种不放弃的精神真是令人感动，你知道吗？菲兰德和菲莉亚根本不值得你这样付出，毕竟他们一生都在为自己谋利，而不是为他人着想。不过，我觉得这样做对你来说并不会有什么好处……
            
            难道你终于要放弃这个‘合理的神明’设定了吗？是雷电会降临，还是火与硫磺会出现呢？”

“不，我亲爱的客人。我只是想提醒您：您还没有摧毁我的据点；根据我作为神明的身份所赋予我的权利，我完全有资格让这些王室兄弟姐妹留在这里。 很好，让我再重复一遍：我是秘密、知识与魔法的女神。我秘密地保存了一种独特魔法的知识。你是否否认这一点？
rows.raw:
'
            "As unfortunate as it may be, I'm finding fault after fault in your arguments," you say. "Didn't you just claim that wraiths enter quite the stupor after such a heavy feeding? Wasn't that why you said you could enter and walk amidst the convocation unmolested?"

            "Hmm..."
            
            "Keeping track of lies becomes increasingly hard as one is forced to keep doing so in order to cover up previous falsehoods. Maybe if you wish to keep the upper hand here, it would be best to come clean and tell us the truth. It's much easier."
            
            Nareva cups her chin in her hands. "You really are serious. Your refusal to give up is so touching, you know? Philander and Phyria deserve so much less, considering how much they've lived their lives for themselves, instead of for the benefit of others. However, I don't think it's going to do you any good..."
            
            "Why, are you going to give up the reasonable deity schtick after all? Is this where the lightning bolts come in, or will it be the fire and brimstone?"
            
            "No, my dear guest. I'm simply choosing to remind you that you still haven't taken down my premises: that I'm fully in my right to keep the royal siblings here, as per what my portfolio as a deity demands. Very well, allow me to reiterate: I am the goddess of secrets, of knowledge, and of magic. I have, in secret, preserved the knowledge of a unique form of magic. Do you deny this?"'

rows.original: "Didn't you just say the wraiths were indisposed?"
rows.translation: 你刚才不是说那些幽灵们状态不好吗？
rows.raw: '"Didn\'t you just say the wraiths were indisposed?"'

rows.original: "Was there no other way to preserve them?"
rows.translation: 难道就没有其他办法来保护它们吗？
rows.raw: '"Was there no other way to preserve them?"'

rows.original: "Allow me to be quite clear," Nareva says. "I did not bear witness to the entire scene. By the time I had arrived atop the plateau, the wraiths had already begun their abominable feasting; it was already too late to save the vast majority of those present at the convocation. Much of what I know of what happened beforehand are either though the royal siblings' memories, my own deductions, or several rather careful attempts at divination." Ria looks thoughtful. "So what you're saying is that you came on the scene too late to save everyone." "It was a snap decision I had to make," Nareva replies. "Between you and your brother or a handful of your guests and subjects... it is not an ideal situation to have to decide who lives and who dies, but we all have faced circumstances that have no clean solution. Philander and you held the most value in the moment, so I chose to whisk the both of you into my Dream." "You make it all sound so clinical," Ria remarks dryly. "We must examine the facts of the matter dispassionately, dear."
rows.translation: 让我把话说明白些，”纳雷瓦说道，“我并没有亲眼目睹那一幕。 全部 当我终于到达高原顶端时，那些幽灵们已经开始了它们那令人作呕的盛宴；对于参加这次集会的大多数人来说，已经为时太晚，无法挽救了。关于之前发生的事情，我所知道的大部分内容，要么来自于王室兄弟姐妹的记忆，要么是我的推论，又或者是一些经过仔细推算得出的结果。蕾亚若有所思地说：“所以你的意思是，你赶到现场的时候已经太晚了，无法救出所有人。” “那是一个我必须立刻做出的决定，”纳雷瓦回答道，“是在你和你的兄弟之间，还是在为数不多的宾客和子民之间做出选择。…被迫决定谁该活下来、谁该死去，这确实不是理想的处境，但我们都曾面临过那些没有完美解决方案的困境。在那个时候，菲兰德和你才是最珍贵的存在，因此我选择了将你们俩带入我的梦境之中。你说得听起来太客观、太冷静了，”莉亚干巴巴地评论道。 “亲爱的，我们必须客观地分析事情的真相。

rows.original: "You saw it all? You didn't intervene more than that?"
rows.translation: 你全都看到了？你就只做了这么多吗？
rows.raw: '"You saw it all? You didn\'t intervene more than that?"'

rows.original: "That's a good question," Ander points out. "While I had asked the invited guests to bring interested colleagues, I don't think anyone Father or I had asked to come were friends with the goddess of magic herself. Not knowingly, anyway. That was why I wasn't surprised to see you, [pc.name] — I thought you were simply a friend of a friend." "The convocation was otherwise kept rather secret," Ria adds. "There were no end of rival city-states that'd have loved to get their hands on Ander and me when we were out cold, ruin his little party, perhaps hold us for ransom from Father. And before you ask, none of the invited guests came from those places, either." "Oh, my presence is rather easy to explain," Nareva replies. "Remember when I said demons aren't the only things drawn by large accumulations of magic? I, too was drawn to this place by the mysteries you were working. They were certainly... novel, I could tell as much. I wanted to find out more about this rather innovative approach to spellcraft, and headed for the plateau atop the forest." Ander grins sheepishly, a little of his old demeanour creeping back. "W-why, thank you. I didn't know I was that great, to warrant impressing a goddess with my studies..." "Impressed enough that she's locked us up in her collection for all time," Ria adds. Ander's face falls. "Ah. Yes."
rows.translation: 这是个好问题，”安德指出，“虽然我邀请了那些受邀的宾客带上来感兴趣的同事，但我想，父亲和我邀请来的那些人中，应该没有谁是那位魔法女神的朋友吧。至少他们并不是故意这么做的。因此，看到你出现在那里，我并不感到惊讶。 [pc.name] 我原本以为你只是我一个朋友的朋友而已。” “这次聚会本来也是被严格保密的，”莉亚补充道，“那些与我们敌对的城市国家肯定都想趁我们毫无防备的时候抓住安德尔和我，破坏他的聚会，甚至向我们的父亲索要赎金。 在你问之前，我要说明的是，被邀请来的客人中也没有人来自那些地方。” “哦，我的出席原因其实很容易解释，”纳雷瓦回答道，“还记得我之前说过吗？大量的魔法并不会只吸引恶魔这类生物。 我也是被你们正在研究的这些神秘事物吸引来到这里的。这些方法确实……相当新颖，这一点我看得出来。我想更深入地了解这种富有创新性的法术研究方式，于是便朝着森林上方的高原方向前进了。安德尴尬地笑了笑，他那老一套的举止又有点显露了出来。“为、为什么，谢谢你。我之前都不知道自己…… 那个 太好了，我的学习成果竟然足以让一位女神为之倾倒……” “她被我们深深打动了，以至于决定把我们永远关在她的收藏品里，”莉亚补充道。 安德尔的脸色顿时黯了下来。“啊，原来如此。

rows.original:
Nareva chuckles at that and raises a finger to her plush lips. "Anyone can simply yell protests at fortissimo, my dear [pc.race] guest. If you're not going to behave any differently from either of the siblings, maybe I shouldn't be wasting my time here."

        Grr... she's right, though; you don't have enough information at this point. Surely the time will come when you've all your ducks lined up in a row and you can strike, but until then, you need to keep the goddess talking and learn more about the situation.
rows.translation:
纳雷瓦听到这话轻笑了一声，然后把一根手指放在自己柔软的嘴唇上说道：“亲爱的，任何人都可以用最大的音量大声抗议啊。 [pc.race] 客人：“如果你和那两个兄弟姐妹的行为没有任何不同，那我在这里浪费时间或许真的没有意义。”

哼……她说的没错，目前你确实掌握的信息还不够。总会有那么一天，当你把所有条件都准备妥当时，就可以采取行动了。但在那之前，你得让这位‘女神’继续开口说话，这样才能了解更多关于当前情况的细节。

rows.original: "This is wrong and you know it! You have no right to keep them here!"
rows.translation: 这是不对的，你心里明白这一点！你没有权利把它们留在这里！
rows.raw: '"This is wrong and you know it! You have no right to keep them here!"'

rows.original: Nareva sighs. "Foolish. Brave, but foolish. Despite being obviously wrong, you're still willing to stick your neck out for the siblings... how very brave and romantic. "Unfortunately, romanticism has no place in my realm. Or do you have some way of supporting your assertion?" Silence. "Well then. While I'm gracious, ill-advised outbursts like this are... irritating. I hope you'll keep that in mind for the rest of the conversation. Now, shall we continue?"
rows.translation: 纳雷瓦叹了口气。 愚蠢。虽然勇敢，但确实很愚蠢。明明知道自己是错的，却还是愿意为那些兄弟姐妹挺身而出……真是太勇敢、太浪漫了。 不幸的是，浪漫主义在我的领域里没有立足之地。或者，你有什么办法来支持你的这个观点吗？” 沉默。 “那么好吧。虽然我为人宽厚，但像这样的无端发泄确实……令人恼火。我希望在接下来的谈话中你能记住这一点。现在，我们继续吧？

rows.original:
Nareva sighs. "No, my dear guest, it's not. If you want to speak of fairness, perhaps you'd have better luck with the likes of Lumia; here, such appeals hold no sway, and that is the painful truth. If you've no argument, then perhaps it's better to just give up instead of hammering away ham-fistedly in the hopes that something will give. It's easier on everyone that way."

        "I'm not giving up on Ander and Ria."
        
        "Brave. In that case, I suggest you continue playing by the rules of the game instead of trying to flout them once you think you've enough of a hand to start doing so. It'll be more constructive, don't you think?"
rows.translation:
纳雷瓦叹了口气：“不，我亲爱的客人，事实并非如此。如果你想谈论公平的话，或许去和卢米娅这类人谈会更有成效；在这里，这样的诉求根本没有任何作用，这就是残酷的现实。如果你没有其他论据，那么或许放弃才是更好的选择，而不是固执地坚持下去，指望最终能取得什么结果。 这样对每个人来说都更方便。”

“我不会放弃安德和莉亚。”

“真勇敢。那么，我建议你继续按照游戏规则来玩，而不是等到觉得自己有足够的实力时才试图违反规则。 这样会更有建设性，你不觉得吗？

rows.original: "See? You have no answer." You think a moment longer, then shake your head. "No, I don't. I know better than to attempt to hold an indefensible position." "In that case, why are you fighting so hard for me to release the royal siblings? You've already heard my reasoning; you've already admitted that you can't deny my premises. What good does drawing out the inevitable serve?" "You're trying really hard to convince me to give up, aren't you?" Nareva turns up a corner of her fanged lips in what might be a smile. "It seems like the most prudent course of action." "Not while there's still a chance." "Oh dear, oh dear. How tragic. Sequestering Philander here is the only way to preserve the glory of mirror magic, you know. Even knowing all this, even assuming I acted contrary to my duties and freed him into oblivion and the void, would you really want his legacy to come to naught?" [var0 |Really now, and so soon? Maybe it's time you brought out that other clue... |Damn it, you don't have a good answer for this. To get so far, and yet... maybe you should try a different tack to the conversation, then strike when you've gotten more information... ]
rows.translation: 看到了吧？你根本没有任何反驳的理由。” 你思考了一会儿，然后摇了摇头：“不，我没有。我懂得不要坚持一个毫无辩护余地的立场。” “那么，为什么你还如此坚决地要求我释放那些王室兄弟姐妹呢？ 你都已经听过了我的理由，也承认自己无法反驳我的论点。那么，再拖延下去又有什么意义呢？” “你其实是在竭力说服我放弃吧？纳雷瓦微微勾起带獠牙的嘴唇，那或许算是一种微笑。“看来，这是最谨慎的做法了。” “只要还有机会，就不应该这么做。” “哦，天哪…… 真是太悲剧了。把菲兰德关在这里，才是保护镜像魔法荣耀的唯一办法，你明白的。即便知道了这一切，即便我认为自己的行为违背了职责，将他放逐到遗忘与虚无之中，你真的希望他的传奇就此终结吗？" [var0 |真的现在就要这么快吗？也许是你该拿出那个东西的时候了…… 其他线索... |该死，你对此竟然没有好的解决办法。都走到这一步了，然而……也许你应该尝试换一种谈话方式，等掌握了更多信息后再采取行动…… ]
