rows.original:
You plant your feet firmly on the ground and fold your arms. Staring down Nareva is hard, but you steel yourself and do it anyway; you know you've got her. "See, I'm finding that particular bit of your argument just a little odd. Wasn't it very recently that we were discussing the Well of Memory?"

            Nareva scowls, dropping all pretense at this point. "What of it?"
            
            "While we were talking about how you might have used it to alter memories... I can't help but recall that you mentioned storing the memories of mortals in said artifact, copying them over. Not your own, but those who've been your guests in this Dream of yours."
            
            "That doesn't invalidate —"
            
            "No, it doesn't, but it does call into question why you've been keeping Ander here for so long. You could've waited for him to recover sufficiently, transcribe the entirety of his knowledge to the Well, and then release him and Ria into the afterlife. The question is, why didn't you? As things stand... with a more humane alternative available to you, I find myself forced to conclude that there's some other reason you're keeping the siblings here by your side."
            
            "Oh, really?"
            
            "Yes, really. I don't think you were lying when you said you truly loved Tychris, both the city and the line... which raises the question of why you are keeping Ander and Ria here against their will. Whatever the reason is, it must be quite the heavy one."
            
            Moments tick by in silence. At last, Nareva steeples her fingers and presses them against her forehead, closing her eyes. "You are treading in dangerous territory here. Please, for your own sake, turn back."
            
            "Then you will free Ander and Ria?"
            
            "No."
            
            "Nor will you tell me the true reason you do not wish to release them into whatever afterlife awaits them."
            
            Nareva looks contemplative. Then, at last, "it is not my secret to reveal. Others beyond myself would be implicated, perhaps even endangered by this knowledge."
            
            "But say, if I were to figure it out by myself, a lucky guess... would you be able to confirm or deny the speculations of a mortal?"
            
            "...Maybe. But if you do manage to come to that conclusion, you will never be able to reveal it to anyone who does not already know the truth of the matter."
            
            Now that sounds ominous. For a moment, you wonder if you should indeed press on with this conversation, but the hopeful faces of Ander and Ria looking back at you steel your resolve. Their fate lies in your hands... it's time to enter the endgame.
rows.translation:
你将双足部牢牢地踩在地面上，双臂交叉抱在胸前。凝视着纳雷瓦，这确实是一件困难的事，但你强忍住内心的不安，还是这么做了——因为你知道，你已经掌握了她的把柄。“听着，我觉得你刚才的论点有点奇怪。不是就在不久前，我们还讨论过‘记忆之井’这个话题吗？

            纳雷瓦皱起了眉头，彻底放弃了所有的伪装。“那又怎样？”

“当我们讨论你可能如何利用这件神器来改变记忆的时候……我不由得想起你曾经说过，可以将凡人的记忆存储在这件神器中，将其复制过来。不是你自己的记忆，而是那些曾经来到你的梦境中的访客们的记忆。
            
            但这并不意味着……”

“不，并不意味着，但这确实让人质疑你为什么要把安德留在这里这么久。你本可以等他完全康复后，将他的所有知识传输到‘井’中，然后再让他和莉亚进入来世。问题在于，你为什么没有这么做？既然有更人道的办法可供选择，我不得不认为，你把这对兄妹留在身边，一定还有其他原因。
            
            哦，真的吗？”

“是的，真的。我觉得你说自己真心热爱提克里斯——无论是那座城市还是那里的人民——的时候并没有撒谎……这就引出了一个问题：为什么你要违背安德尔和莉亚的意愿，把他们留在这里呢？无论原因是什么，肯定是非常重要的原因吧。
            
            时间在沉默中悄然流逝。最终，纳雷瓦将手部指交叉放在额头上，闭上了眼睛。“你现在正在踏入危险的领域。为了你自己的安全，请回头吧。”

“那么，你会释放安德和莉亚吗？
            
            不。”

“你也不会告诉我，你真正不愿意让它们进入等待它们的来世的真正原因。”

纳雷瓦陷入沉思，最终说道：“这个秘密并不属于我一个人，如果透露出来，其他人也会受到影响，甚至可能会因此陷入危险。
            
            但是，假设我自己是想出了那个答案，只是凭运气猜对的……你能够证实或否定一个凡人的这种猜测吗？”

“……也许吧。但如果你真的得出了那个结论，你也永远无法向那些还不了解事情真相的人透露它。
            
            这听起来确实有些不妙。有那么一瞬间，你开始怀疑是否真的应该继续进行这场对话，但安德和莉亚那充满希望的眼神让你重新坚定了决心。他们的命运掌握在你手部中……是时候进入最后阶段了。
rows.raw:
'
            You plant your feet firmly on the ground and fold your arms. Staring down Nareva is hard, but you steel yourself and do it anyway; you know you've got her. "See, I'm finding that particular bit of your argument just a little odd. Wasn't it very recently that we were discussing the Well of Memory?"

            Nareva scowls, dropping all pretense at this point. "What of it?"
            
            "While we were talking about how you might have used it to alter memories... I can't help but recall that you mentioned storing the memories of mortals in said artifact, copying them over. Not your own, but those who've been your guests in this Dream of yours."
            
            "That doesn't invalidate —"
            
            "No, it doesn't, but it does call into question why you've been keeping Ander here for so long. You could've waited for him to recover sufficiently, transcribe the entirety of his knowledge to the Well, and then release him and Ria into the afterlife. The question is, why didn't you? As things stand... with a more humane alternative available to you, I find myself forced to conclude that there's some other reason you're keeping the siblings here by your side."
            
            "Oh, really?"
            
            "Yes, really. I don't think you were lying when you said you truly loved Tychris, both the city and the line... which raises the question of why you are keeping Ander and Ria here against their will. Whatever the reason is, it must be quite the heavy one."
            
            Moments tick by in silence. At last, Nareva steeples her fingers and presses them against her forehead, closing her eyes. "You are treading in dangerous territory here. Please, for your own sake, turn back."
            
            "Then you will free Ander and Ria?"
            
            "No."
            
            "Nor will you tell me the true reason you do not wish to release them into whatever afterlife awaits them."
            
            Nareva looks contemplative. Then, at last, "it is not my secret to reveal. Others beyond myself would be implicated, perhaps even endangered by this knowledge."
            
            "But say, if I were to figure it out by myself, a lucky guess... would you be able to confirm or deny the speculations of a mortal?"
            
            "...Maybe. But if you do manage to come to that conclusion, you will never be able to reveal it to anyone who does not already know the truth of the matter."
            
            Now that sounds ominous. For a moment, you wonder if you should indeed press on with this conversation, but the hopeful faces of Ander and Ria looking back at you steel your resolve. Their fate lies in your hands... it's time to enter the endgame.'

"At the very least, I have been calmer than Phyria here, or you for that matter, my dear guest. Phyria... well at least she has her innate temperament as an excuse. I'm not exactly sure the same holds for you."

        "Psssh."
        
        Nareva shrugs. "You're not the first mortals to rage in my face, blaming me for the woes for the world. After a while, such emotional outbursts just blend into one another and become rather indistinguishable.
        
        "Let me know when you're done, so we can continue the conversation."

至少，我在这里比菲莉亚要冷静得多，当然，也比你冷静，我亲爱的客人。菲莉亚……嗯，至少她可以以天生的性格为借口。不过我不太确定你也能用这个理由来解释自己的行为。”

        等你忙完告诉我，这样我们就可以继续谈话了。

rows.original: "In either case, yes. Given how the situation had progressed... what options I had were limited. Your half-brother and you were already rather gnawed on at that point, but not fatally, so I was able to reconstitute your selves after a fashion. Stitch up your metaphysical wounds, as it were." Ander swallows hard at that. "You didn't... do anything to us?" Nareva thinks a moment, then shakes her head. "No, I wouldn't have altered your memories or implanted new ones. Firstly, I needed them as they were; I was not about to touch your mind for fear of damaging the very expertise of mirror magic I was attempting to preserve. Secondly, if I had altered your memories, do you think I'd have allowed dear Phyria to remain so belligerent towards me, or for you to have disturbing gaps in your recollections of this place?" Ander frowns. "It's true that when I first met [pc.name], I couldn't quite recall the events of the day..." "You and your sister have been healing from your spiritual wounds in this place for quite some time, and even so, neither of you are fully recovered." Nareva shrugs and shifts her serpentine coils. "Truth be told, you may never recuperate fully, just as an old soldier may always be lame from an old injury. That you have progressed as far as you have is testament to the strength of your souls."
rows.translation: 无论哪种情况，都是这样。考虑到事情的发展进程……我的选择其实非常有限。在那个时候，你和你同父异母的兄弟已经受到了相当大的影响，但还不至于致命，所以我才能够以某种方式让你们恢复原状。可以说，我是帮你们治愈了那些‘精神上的伤痕’。” 安德听完这话，艰难地咽了口唾沫：“你没有…… 做 这对我们来说有什么意义吗？” 纳雷瓦思考了一会儿，然后摇了摇头。“不，我不会改变你的记忆，也不会植入新的记忆。首先，我需要你原有的记忆；我不敢触碰你的思维，因为我害怕这样会破坏我试图保护的镜像魔法这种独特的技巧。其次，如果我…… 拥有过 它改变了你的记忆，你难道认为我会允许亲爱的菲莉亚一直对我如此敌对，或者让你对这个地方的记忆出现如此混乱的空白吗？” 安德皱起了眉头。“的确，当我第一次遇见…… [pc.name]我实在想不起当天发生了什么……” “你和你的妹妹在这个地方已经花了很长时间来治愈你们心灵上的伤痛，但即便如此，你们俩也还没有完全恢复。”纳雷瓦耸了耸肩，她那蜿蜒盘曲的身体微微动了动。“说实话，你们可能永远也无法完全康复，就像那些老兵一样，他们可能永远都会因为旧伤而行动不便。但你们能够取得如今的进步，已经证明了你们灵魂的强大。

rows.original:
"Is it? I wouldn't know."

        You scratch your chin and quirk a corner of your mouth upwards. "I'm just finding it curious, that's all. Ander over here never mentioned what he thought you did to him, yet your first response was to deny altering his memories. Neither do I remember you being able to read minds..."
        
        "Mm-hm..."
        
        "A more reasonable response to his question would be to ask what he thought you did to him while he was indisposed," you continue. "So, why exactly did you latch onto that particular thread of thought?"
        
        "Because it was something I could very well have done, and in fact, was tempted to do in the years he and Phyria have been lying here by my side," Nareva admits with a small sigh. "If only to avoid a situation much like the one we find ourselves in right now. However, after having been friends with the House of Tychris for a while, I decided against doing so after the first decade he'd been here. I owe him that much for bringing true color into my existence; with all that's happened since the day I came across his little convocation, I can't deny that things have been interesting."
        
        "Interesting," Ria mumbles grouchily.
        
        "That, and of course, risking damaging the treasure the prince held in his mind were I to alter its contents. So yes, it was my guilt at having been tempted to do such a thing that provoked that particular response. Take that for what you will."
        
        Ander grimaces. "And we have nothing to go on but your word."
        
        "And the fact that the both of you are questioning me, when if I had gone through with the temptation I'd have simply erased all of your inconvenient recollections. Philander, I don't blame you for being suspicious of me, but the facts are what they are. Surely you realize as much from your arguments with your father."
rows.translation:
是吗？我倒不太清楚。”

你挠了挠下巴，嘴角微微上扬：“我只是觉得这件事有点奇怪而已。这里的安德从没提到你对他做了什么，而你的第一反应却是否认自己改动了他的记忆。我也不记得你以前有过读心术的能力……
        
        嗯……”

“对于他的问题，一个更合理的回应应该是问他，他认为在你他身体不适的时候，你对他做了什么，”你继续说道。“那么，你究竟为什么偏偏抓住这个特定的思路不放呢？因为这是我完全有可能做的事情，事实上，在他和菲莉亚这些年一直陪伴在我身边的时候，我也确实有过这样的冲动，”纳雷瓦轻叹着承认道，“只为了避免陷入我们现在这样的境地罢了。 然而，在与提克里斯家族成为朋友一段时间后，在他来到这里的第一个十年里，我最终决定不那么做了。他为我带来了如此多的精彩与乐趣，因此我欠他这个人情；自从我遇到了他的那个小聚会以来，发生的一切确实让我的生活变得十分有趣，这一点我不得不承认。"
        
        有意思，”莉亚闷闷不乐地嘟囔道。

“当然，如果我改变了王子心中所珍视的那些东西，就有可能损坏它们。所以，没错，正是我被这种诱惑所驱使，才导致了那样的反应。你们爱怎么理解就怎么理解吧。
        
        安德皱起了眉头。“而我们除了你的话之外，没有任何其他依据。”

“更何况，你们两个人都在质疑我。如果我真的屈服于那种诱惑，那么我早就把你们那些麻烦的回忆全部抹去了。菲兰德，我并不怪你对我产生怀疑，但事实就是如此。想必你在和你父亲的争论中也意识到了这一点吧。

rows.original:
"Oh, of course I am. Wouldn't you make the best case for yourself in any debate? If my words sound reasonable and sympathetic, even after closer inspection and thought... maybe it's just that my position makes sense. If you're going to convince other people of what you're saying, isn't making yourself appeal to them part and parcel of that?"

        "I wouldn't know about that," Ria mutters. "Ander's always been able to make people nod along with him despite everything coming out of his mouth being nothing but empty words. It's always been up to me to step in and rein in his bullshit before his mouth gets ahead of him."
        
        Nareva shrugs. "Ah, well. Eloquence can get you quite far, but in the end a single perceptive mind peeling apart your words will be sufficient to get at the substance beneath. I think the term your father used to describe it was... hmm... bafflegarble."
        
        Ria swallows hard and winces.
        
        "But returning to the topic at hand, [pc.name], if you have a problem with my arguments, please attack their substance instead of how they make you feel." Nareva steeples her fingers and smiles down at you over them. "I think you'll have considerably more success that way."
        
        Gaaaah. To think you're being lectured by her even as she's stonewalling you. Then again, this far into the conversation, you should have known better than to try this tack with her...
rows.translation:
哦，当然会了。在任何辩论中，人们不都会尽力为自己争取最有利的立场吗？如果我的言论听起来合理且富有同情心，即使经过仔细推敲和思考之后也是如此……也许只是因为我的观点本身就有道理罢了。如果你想说服别人接受你的观点，那么让自己显得更有吸引力，不正是其中不可或缺的一部分吗？这个我就不清楚了，”莉亚低声说道，“安德总是能够让别人跟着他的节奏走，尽管他说出的话全都是一些空洞的废话。每次都得由我来出面，阻止他再继续说那些胡话，否则他的话就会超出他的控制范围了。纳雷瓦耸了耸肩：“啊，好吧。雄辩确实能让你走得很远，但最终，只要有一个善于洞察的人仔细分析你的话语，就足以看清其中的实质。我想你父亲用来形容这种情况的词就是……嗯……真是让人摸不着头脑。”

莉亚艰难地咽了口唾沫，脸上露出痛苦的表情。

“不过，还是回到正题上来吧。 [pc.name]如果你对我的论点有意见，那就请针对论点的实质进行反驳，而不是纠结于它们让你产生了什么样的感受。”纳雷瓦将手指交叉在一起，透过这些手指微笑着看着你，“我觉得这样你会取得更大的成功。”

rows.original: At your question, Nareva's smile fades and she considers you for several moments. At last, she sighs and curls the tip of her serpentine tail about herself. "Normally, I would refuse to answer, but given the circumstances I suppose you deserve to know. The royal siblings have earned that right, if nothing else, and you..." "Yes?" "Never mind. Somewhere within this dream, there is an artifact of my own creation, known as the Well of Memory. I believe I've mentioned it previously in this conversation." "Yes, you have." Nareva nods. "Its primary purpose is to serve as an archive — a place where I could store my remembrances in perfect detail, to be retrieved later on as needed. The times I've had with the House of Tychris... I knew they would eventually fade if I just tried to keep them in my mind. Hence... that was my impetus for fashioning the well, at any rate. "Over time, I've added to its functionalities, and it now serves me inasmuch Philander's private collection served him. A library of the world's secrets, kept so securely that even I have lost track of all the details... the things I've learned in these centuries have been faithfully transcribed to the well, and that of a number of mortals who've voluntarily submitted to the procedure." "And where does the memory alteration come in?" Ander asks. "You see, while I don't mind mortals knowing of this place, the knowledge of how to get to my Dream is another matter altogether. While I don't mind entertaining the occasional guest, I'm not enthused with the idea of a steady stream of petitioners lining up to beg me for the knowledge of some trivial secret or the other. For those who've found their way to my door on their own... I've regrettably had to wipe their minds of that knowledge. "That means," Nareva continues, looking straight at you, "when we're done here, my dear guest, you won't be able to return in the same fashion. Not without me bringing you here, that is." Hmm. Ander's rather animated by this whole train of thought, and as he delves into a rather heated discussion with the goddess, you pause to take a moment as to what's been said. Interesting... what stood out to you in the tail end of this conversation, though, was the capabilities of this well, especially where they pertained to normal people. That might serve as a clue later on...
rows.translation: 听到你的问题，纳雷瓦的笑容消失了，她沉思了好一会儿。最终，她叹了口气，将自己那条蜿蜒曲折的尾巴末端绕在身上。“通常情况下，我会拒绝回答这个问题的，但考虑到目前的情形，我想你确实有权利知道。 这些王室兄弟姐妹至少是凭这个理由才获得这种权利的，而你…… “是吗？” “算了。在这个梦境的某个地方，有一件由我亲手创造的神器，被称为‘记忆之井’。我想我之前在这段对话中已经提到过它了。是的，你确实有。” 纳雷瓦点了点头。 它的主要用途是作为一个档案库——一个我可以将所有回忆以极其详尽的形式保存其中的地方，以后需要时可以随时取出来查看。那些与泰克里斯之屋共度的时光……我知道，如果只是把它们记在脑海里，最终这些回忆还是会逐渐淡忘的。因此……至少，这就是我建造这个‘井’的初衷。 随着时间的推移，我不断为它增添新的功能，现在它对我的作用，就如同菲兰德尔的私人藏书对他而言一样。这是一个储存着世间秘密的图书馆，这些秘密被保存得如此严密，以至于就连我也已经记不清所有的细节了……这几个世纪以来我所了解到的各种知识，都被忠实地记录在了这个‘井’中，同时也有一些自愿接受这种仪式的凡人也将自己的知识记录在了其中。” “那么，记忆的改变又是如何发生的呢？”安德问道。 你看，虽然我并不介意凡人知道…… 的 这个地方，以及如何获得通往我梦想之路的知识，则是另一回事了。虽然我不介意偶尔招待一些访客，但我实在不乐意有一大群人排队向我乞求那些琐碎的秘密知识。而对于那些自己找到我的人……很遗憾，我不得不让他们忘记那些知识。 这意味着，”纳雷瓦直视着你的眼睛继续说道，“当我们在这里的事情完成后，我亲爱的客人，你就再也无法以原来的方式返回去了。除非我再次带你来这里。” 嗯，安德对这一系列的想法显得相当兴奋，而他与这位女神展开了激烈的讨论。你则暂停了一下，试图理解他们刚才说了些什么。 有趣……不过，在这次对话的结尾，真正让你印象深刻的是这个“井”的各种功能，尤其是那些与普通人相关的功能。 这以后或许能成为一个线索……
rows.raw: ' At your question, Nareva's smile fades and she considers you for several moments. At last, she sighs and curls the tip of her serpentine tail about herself. "Normally, I would refuse to answer, but given the circumstances I suppose you deserve to know. The royal siblings have earned that right, if nothing else, and you..." "Yes?" "Never mind. Somewhere within this dream, there is an artifact of my own creation, known as the Well of Memory. I believe I've mentioned it previously in this conversation." "Yes, you have." Nareva nods. "Its primary purpose is to serve as an archive — a place where I could store my remembrances in perfect detail, to be retrieved later on as needed. The times I've had with the House of Tychris... I knew they would eventually fade if I just tried to keep them in my mind. Hence... that was my impetus for fashioning the well, at any rate. "Over time, I've added to its functionalities, and it now serves me inasmuch Philander's private collection served him. A library of the world's secrets, kept so securely that even I have lost track of all the details... the things I've learned in these centuries have been faithfully transcribed to the well, and that of a number of mortals who've voluntarily submitted to the procedure." "And where does the memory alteration come in?" Ander asks. "You see, while I don't mind mortals knowing of this place, the knowledge of how to get to my Dream is another matter altogether. While I don't mind entertaining the occasional guest, I'm not enthused with the idea of a steady stream of petitioners lining up to beg me for the knowledge of some trivial secret or the other. For those who've found their way to my door on their own... I've regrettably had to wipe their minds of that knowledge. "That means," Nareva continues, looking straight at you, "when we're done here, my dear guest, you won't be able to return in the same fashion. Not without me bringing you here, that is." Hmm. Ander's rather animated by this whole train of thought, and as he delves into a rather heated discussion with the goddess, you pause to take a moment as to what's been said. Interesting... what stood out to you in the tail end of this conversation, though, was the capabilities of this well, especially where they pertained to normal people. That might serve as a clue later on... '

rows.original:
"In my capacity as goddess of magic, yes. Believe it or not, I do not mysteriously receive knowledge of new spells as they are formulated; part of my portfolio involves keeping abreast of new magics as they are discovered. It gives me an excuse to interact with mortals on a more casual footing, you see. Many are more than willing to share their discoveries, like Philander here."
        
        "And if they're not?" you ask.
        
        "Well, in that case I have other means at my disposal. Ah... I readily confess that my vigilance has not been as great as it ought to be at times. What happened at Estelore... I share the blame for that particular disaster. But in any case, yes, I wanted to discover more about the prince's new school of magic."
        
        Ander thinks a moment. "I don't believe I ever invited a goddess to the convocation, and I doubt any of the guests were familiar enough with one, even if possibly disguised."
        
        "The prince is right that I received no invitation."
        
        "How, then..."
        
        "Some creatures are possessed of senses not available to you, my dear prince. For example, bats are able to navigate quite well in the dark, and fish are able to sense minute traces of lightning currents generated by other fish. In a similar manner, wraiths are able to sense the presence of magic, raw, untrammeled power... and so am I. Rather than requiring a spell to be able to detect its presence like you would, it is in our natures. You did work some rather impressive magic, did you not?"
        
        "I... I'd wanted to impress my guests in my opening speech... a dazzling demonstration of what they could expect to learn in their time with me."
        
        Nareva smiles and shrugs. "There we have your answer, [pc.name]. Are you satisfied now?"
rows.translation:
作为魔法女神，我的职责确实如此。信不信由你，我并不是在新的法术被创造出来的瞬间就神秘地获得相关知识的；我的职责之一就是及时了解那些新发现的魔法。这样，我就有借口以更随意的方式与凡人交流了。很多人都很乐意分享他们的发现，就像这里的菲兰德一样。
        
        那么，如果他们没有呢？”你问道。

“嗯，那样的话，我还有其他办法可以动用。啊……我必须承认，有时候我的警惕性确实没有达到应有的水平。在埃斯托洛尔发生的事情……我对那场灾难也负有责任。但无论如何，我的确想要了解更多关于那位王子新建立的魔法学校的情况。
        
        安德思考了一会儿，说道：“我想我从来没邀请过女神参加这次聚会，而且我也怀疑在场的宾客中，没有人真正认识女神，即使她们可能伪装过了。”

“王子说得对，我确实没有收到任何邀请。”

“那么，这到底是怎么回事……
        
        亲爱的王子，有些生物拥有你所没有的感觉能力。例如，蝙蝠能够在暗影中自如地导航，而鱼类则能够感知其他鱼类释放出的微弱电场信号。同样地，幽灵们能够感知魔力的存在——那种原始而强大的力量……而我也是如此。与我们不同，你需要借助咒语才能察觉魔力的存在，而这对我们来说却是与生俱来的能力。你刚才施展的魔法，确实相当厉害，不是吗？
        
        我……我本来想在开场演讲中给各位宾客留下深刻印象……展示一下他们在与我共事期间能够学到些什么。”

纳雷瓦微笑着耸了耸肩：“这就是你的答案了。 [pc.name]现在你满意了吗？

rows.original: "It's a little strange that the wraiths didn't notice your approach," you point out. "They must've been quite sensitive to magical powers in order to converge on the convocation all at once. Why didn't they sense you, then?" "Some people have better eyes, others have better noses, so on and so forth," comes the reply. "The bulk of the forest's inhabitants at the time were Wyld and Pale Elves, and their practice of the art is largely druidic, not arcane. Philander's convocation would have lit up the forest like a lighthouse beacon; dazzling and hard to miss." "Even so..." you think a moment and shake your head. "[pc.bg arcanist scholar acolyte |I don't need to see the power pouring off you right now, because I can feel it. Ria may not be as sensitive as her brother, but I'm sure Ander recognizes magic when he feels it. |I don't have that kind of background in magic, but just you standing there makes my [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] tingle, and it's not nerves. I'm sure Ander can shed some more light on the subject. ]" Ander hesitates, looking between you and Nareva, then nods warily. "As accomplished a mage as I am, I don't think the convocation with all its wonders would've been able to mask your approach." "Of course, I had intended to attend your lectures while suitably disguised, Philander. Wearing the shape of a frost-tailed salamander would have been of little use if my aura gave me away. You don't think I can't suppress my presence whenever I wish, do you? Under ordinary circumstances, perhaps there was a chance the wraiths might have sensed me nevertheless... but it was a sliver of a chance to begin with. "Besides, by the time I was on the scene, it was too late — the monsters had already begun their feasting."

rows.original: "Ah... well, you've got me there. Guilty as charged. Although to be honest, I don't imagine Philander would have objected very strongly if he'd known I'd slipped in, would he?" To your surprise, you see the prince's cheeks flush. "I... I can't deny that I would've been honored to have such an eminent personage. There is only one step up for royalty to receive in terms of dignitaries, and that's divinity itself." "In either case, I did not intend to cause any disruption of the convocation. Quite the opposite, in fact. So yes, while I may have snuck in without the prince's permission, since it resulted in both his sister and him being saved from oblivion, I think it was for the better, no?" Oh, now you see her game. She's admitting the little passable faults to divert attention from the big things that she's hiding, you're sure of it. Either way, you need to stay on track here and avoid wasting precious time; while this might have been a perfectly valid question to ask in and of itself, it wasn't connected to the bigger picture. You need to always keep your goal in mind here... The game is stepping up. Keep pace, or fall behind!

rows.original: "If you'd like to know more, I'll be more than happy to indulge you." With that Nareva launches into a long-winded and highly technical explanation of how people and animals perceive the world about them, and how this happens in a myriad of ways. [pc.bg scholar acolyte arcanist |Even with your learned background, you're still having a good deal of trouble keeping up with the goddess, especially when she's so enthusiastic about it. |There's no way you understand anything of what she's saying, most of it going straight over your head; you don't even know half the words she's using. ] Ander, on his part, is completely rapt by Nareva's explanation; you can see the gears whirring away in his mind at top speed. "I didn't think of it that way, but now that it all makes sense, I'm flabbergasted at how the simple truth evaded me," he mutters. "Well, that's something." Nareva smiles. "I am glad to be of service." Damn it. rows.raw: '"What about these senses? How do they work?"'

rows.original: "Hm? Whatever do you mean?" "You said that under ordinary circumstances, there was a chance the wraiths might have discovered you, right?" Nareva frowns. "That is correct." "In that case, what were the unordinary circumstances that made you so confident that you'd escape the wraiths' notice?" "Hmm. Hmm... like I said, there was the whole matter of the grandiose display with which he invited his guests; that would certainly mask residual traces of my presence I had missed..." You shake your head. "You really need to socialise with mortals more, if you want to be convincing when you play dumb; goddess or not, you're clearly not acting on-the-level here! Magic at a magical convocation would certainly be considered ordinary, so I'll ask again: why were you so confident the wraiths wouldn't notice you?" Nareva pauses a moment, her lips twisting as if unsure whether to take offense or smile. At last, she settles on the latter. "...Clever. I like it. Very well, then — when I arrived on the scene, the wraiths were already in the process of feeding on Philander's poor guests. Now then, wraiths are beings of void and blankness; to taste desires, emotions and their like is much akin to giving rich chocolate to someone who has never tasted anything more flavorful than cabbage soup in their lives. That's why they're momentarily stupefied by the act, addled by the sheer rush of intense, addictive experience. "They might have vaguely noticed me had I chosen to approach unconcealed, but as I was I could walk straight into their midst and snatch the royal siblings from the jaws of oblivion. Doubly so when they'd just devoured hedonists of the glorious kind the prince prefers to keep company with, with all their memories of every indulgence the Belharan Empire could bring to bear." Hmm... so Nareva was quite sure the wraiths were in too deep a stupor to have noticed her no matter what she did... That might serve as a clue.
rows.translation: 嗯？你是什么意思？” “你刚才说过，在正常情况下，那些幽灵有可能发现你，对吧？” 纳雷瓦皱起了眉头。“没错。” “那么，当时究竟发生了什么？ 不在那种普通情况下，你究竟是怎么有如此大的信心，能够逃过那些幽灵的注意的呢？” “嗯……就像我之前说的，他邀请客人们时所举行的那种盛大仪式，肯定能够掩盖我可能留下的任何痕迹……” 你摇了摇头：“如果你想装傻装得让人信服的话，真的需要多和凡人交往一些。不管你是不是女神，这次你的表现显然太不自然了！使用魔法来…… 神奇的 召集会议这样的举动肯定不会引起他们的注意，所以我想再问一次：你为什么如此有把握，认为那些幽灵不会发现你呢？” 纳雷瓦停顿了片刻，她的嘴唇微微扭曲，似乎不确定自己是该感到生气还是应该微笑。最终，她选择了微笑。 ……真聪明。我喜欢这个想法。那么，当我赶到现场时，那些幽灵已经开始吞噬菲兰德那些可怜的客人了。要知道，幽灵本质上是虚无与空白的存在；对于它们来说，品尝欲望、情感之类的东西，就如同给一个一生中从未尝过比卷心菜汤更美味的东西的人赠送浓郁的巧克力一样。正因为如此，它们会在这一过程中暂时陷入恍惚状态，被那种强烈而令人上瘾的体验所震撼。 如果我选择光明正大地接近他们，他们或许会隐约注意到我的存在；但就我的行事方式而言，我完全可以直接走进他们中间，把那对皇室兄妹从遗忘的深渊中拯救出来。更何况，当时他们刚刚吞噬了那些王子最喜欢结交的享乐主义者——那些人拥有贝尔哈兰帝国所能提供的一切奢华享受，他们的记忆也都被彻底抹去了。” 嗯……看来纳雷瓦非常确信，那些幽灵们正处于极度昏沉的状态中，无论她做什么，他们都根本不会注意到她…… 这或许能提供一个线索。

        "It's not unwarranted... but perhaps I need to ask more," you say. "I just need to figure out what."
        
        "Take your time," Nareva replies with a smile and just the barest hint of a jibe. "We have plenty."

rows.original:
With you having come this far, perhaps it's time to take stock of the situation once more. While you've no way to deny that Nareva is keeping Ander and Ria in this place to preserve the former's knowledge of mirror magic, you're certain that it can't be the primary reason they're here. Looks like your ultimate goal still hasn't changed — if you can find the true reason for the 'mander siblings' captivity, that's got to be the final blow you need to get the goddess to relent.

    This is the endgame... Nareva is only going to get more evasive from here on out, and more inclined to cut off the conversation should you stumble. The path to the truth behind all of this exists, but you can barely glimpse it from where you are. Still, it's more than you had before, and that's got to count for something.

    Well, then. It's time to see where this road takes you, no matter how dark the destination.
rows.translation:
既然你已经走了这么远，或许现在是时候再次审视一下当前的形势了。虽然你无法否认Nareva将Ander和Ria关在这里，是为了利用前者对镜像魔法的了解，但你肯定知道，这不可能是他们被关在这里的唯一原因。 看来你的最终目标依然没有改变——只要你能找到“曼德尔姐妹”被囚禁的真正原因，那就一定能给女神以致命一击，让她改变主意。

这才是最终阶段……从现在开始，纳雷瓦只会变得更加躲躲藏藏，而且一旦你犯错，她就会更加倾向于中断对话。 通往这一切背后真相的道路确实存在，但从你现在的位置来看，几乎无法窥见它的踪迹。不过，这已经比你之前所拥有的要多多了，这一点总归是值得肯定的。

那么，好吧。是时候看看这条路会将你引向何方了，无论终点处有多么暗影。

rows.original:
"Given our conversation so far," you say, "I find myself forced to conclude that there's little rationale behind keeping Ander and Ria here."

        Nareva clicks her tongue. "Oh, really."
        
        "It's true that you are acting in your rights, and within your portfolio and domain as a deity. And yet... you're going to far too much trouble to keep two rebellious siblings here. Given that you're capable of transcribing mortals' memories to this artifact of yours, the question still remains as to why it can't be done now. Even if Ander and Ria were too injured to do so before, they appear quite themselves now."
        
        "Now then, my dear guest, let's not mince our words. What exactly are you saying here?"

根据我们迄今为止的谈话，”你说，“我不得不认为，将安德和莉亚留在这里其实并没有什么合理的理由。”

纳雷瓦吐了吐舌头：“哦，是吗。”

“的确，你的行为是在行使你的权利，也在你作为神明的职责范围和领域之内。 然而……你们为了留下这两个叛逆的兄弟姐妹，竟然费了这么大的劲。既然你们有能力将凡人的记忆转移到你们的这件神器上，那么为什么现在还不能这么做呢？这个疑问依然存在。 虽然之前安德和莉亚伤得太重，无法行动，但现在他们看起来已经恢复得差不多了。”

“那么，亲爱的客人，我们就直说吧。你到底想表达什么意思？

rows.original: "How surprising," you say. "I'm also getting tired of having to repeat myself — your own words have long since given the game away. I don't know what your reason is, but it damn well isn't the preservation of mirror magic! Since by your own admission you're not taking it seriously at the slightest, it can't be more than a cover story! "So now, let's talk about Ander and Ria, shall we?" Nareva sighs. "Some of you mortals are so full of vigor and vitality... intent on living fast and recklessly, just like Phyria here. You'll regret this, soon enough." "I'll be the one to decide that." "...I didn't mean that as a threat, you know. You're not thinking this through properly — there are things that are better left buried. Even were I to release Philander and Phyria, it still wouldn't change anything. You've come this far, but it's not too late to turn back." "I refuse." "...Why?" "Because then Ander and Ria will be here for all eternity without ever knowing why!" "I get it. I'm beginning to understand what kind of person you truly are, [pc.name]. It really is such a pity. If it had been any other quest for knowledge, I would've accepted it... such brilliance all gone to waste."

rows.original:
Nareva thinks a moment. "That question's rather vague. Mind if you clarified what you meant?"

        "I refer to not just the royal siblings, but also what remained of the convocation. Wasn't there anything else that you could've done to help?"
        
        "In retrospect, probably, but one has far better judgement of what is a good decision and what is not in hindsight. I chose to save the most likely and valuable targets — Philander and Phyria — because there was a chance they might recover from their spiritual injuries, regardless of how traumatic they were."
        
        "So, there was no hope for the other members of the convocation?"
        
        "I am sure that these are but legends to you at this point, [pc.name], but speaking as someone who was there when it happened... wraiths are ravenous creatures, and they are quite thorough in cleaning their plates. The victim's soul and personality are first to go, and what remains is but a shell, capable of little more than animalistic instincts under its own power. By the time I appeared on the scene, the outer circle of sleepers had already been fully consumed; it was too late to save any of them. The spirit, as the body, can be dealt mortal wounds from which one can never recover; people are capable of doing such to each other, though in a less direct fashion."
rows.translation:
纳雷瓦思考了一会儿，说道：“这个问题有点模糊。你能不能具体说明一下你的意思呢？”

“我指的不仅仅是王室兄弟姐妹，还包括那次集会中剩下的其他人。难道你们没有其他办法可以提供帮助吗？事后看来，或许确实如此。因为事后人们总是能更清楚地判断什么才是正确的决定，什么不是。我选择拯救那些最有可能存活下来、也最有价值的目标——菲兰德和菲莉亚，因为它们有恢复的可能，无论那些精神创伤有多严重。那么，这次集会中的其他成员就没有任何希望了吗？”

“我敢肯定，对你们来说，这些只不过是一些传说罢了。 [pc.name]但作为一个亲身经历过那些事情的人来说……怨灵确实是极其贪婪的生物，它们会彻底吞噬掉猎物的一切。受害者的灵魂与人格会首先被夺走，剩下的只不过是一个空壳，这种空壳在失去原有意识之后，所能依靠的也只有动物般的本能罢了。 当我赶到现场时，那些处于外围的睡眠者早已全部被吞噬殆尽；此时再想拯救他们也已经为时太晚。灵魂与身体一样，也会受到致命的伤害，而这些伤害往往会导致永远无法恢复的后果；人类有时也会对自己施加这样的伤害，只不过方式更为隐晦罢了。"

The spirit, as the body, can be dealt mortal wounds from which one can never recover; people are capable of doing such to each other, though in a less direct fashion."'

rows.original: "Was there truly nothing else that could be done?"
rows.translation: 真的没有其他办法可以尝试了吗？
rows.raw: '"Was there truly nothing else that could be done?"'

rows.original:
Nareva chuckles at that and raises a finger to her plush lips. "Anyone can simply yell protests at fortissimo, my dear [pc.race] guest. If you're not going to behave any differently from either of the siblings, maybe I shouldn't be wasting my time here."

            Grr... she's right, though; you don't have enough information at this point. Surely the time will come when you've all your ducks lined up in a row and you can strike, but until then, you need to keep the goddess talking and learn more about the situation.
rows.translation:
纳雷瓦听到这话轻笑了一声，然后把手指放在自己柔软的嘴唇上说道：“亲爱的，任何人都可以用最大的音量大声抗议啊。 [pc.race] 客人：“如果你表现得和那两个兄弟姐妹没有任何不同，或许我在这里浪费时间也是徒劳的。”

哼……她说的没错，目前你确实掌握的信息还不够。总会有那么一天，当你把所有条件都准备妥当时，就可以采取行动了。但在那之前，你得让这位‘女神’继续开口说话，这样才能了解更多关于当前情况的细节。
rows.raw:
"
            Nareva chuckles at that and raises a finger to her plush lips. "Anyone can simply yell protests at fortissimo, my dear [pc.race] guest. If you're not going to behave any differently from either of the siblings, maybe I shouldn't be wasting my time here."

            Grr... she's right, though; you don't have enough information at this point. Surely the time will come when you've all your ducks lined up in a row and you can strike, but until then, you need to keep the goddess talking and learn more about the situation."

rows.original:
Nareva winces. The serpentine goddess' fanged lips are set into a thin, straight line, and her gaze wanders away from yours as she clears her throat.

        "Haven't you already come to your conclusion, my dear guest? Just say it, and there's no need to dress it up. We're all listening."
        
        "You're sure you want me to say it out loud?"
        
        A sigh. "I have resolved myself to this; it was bound to happen sooner or later. Now, out with it already."
rows.translation:
纳雷瓦微微皱起了眉头。这位身形如蛇的女神的獠牙紧闭，嘴唇绷成一条细长的直线，她的目光从你身上移开，轻轻清了清嗓子。

“亲爱的客人，你难道还没有得出结论吗？直接说出来吧，没必要拐弯抹角。我们都在听着呢。”

“你确定真的想让我把话讲出来吗？”

“唉……我早就下定决心了；这件事迟早会发生的。现在，就把话讲吧。

'

        "Haven't you already come to your conclusion, my dear guest? Just say it, and there's no need to dress it up. We're all listening."
        
        "You're sure you want me to say it out loud?"
        
        A sigh. "I have resolved myself to this; it was bound to happen sooner or later. Now, out with it already."'

rows.original: "Whaaaaat?" Ander and Ria cry out in unison. For all their differences, they can be really similar at times... "Well, goddess? All that really remains is for you to admit or deny it." "..." "Well?" "...Yes, yes, you are a smart one, [pc.name]. A worthy successor to Philander's legacy." Nareva sniffles a little and wipes the tears from her eyes. "There's no point denying it now. Yes, you are right. I am a wraith." This wasn't quite the truth you were hoping to uncover, but even so... it's over.
rows.translation: 什么？！ 安德和莉亚异口同声地叫了出来。尽管他们之间存在很多差异，但有时候他们的想法却出奇地相似…… “那么，女神？现在剩下的就是您承认或者否认这件事了。” “……” “那么？” “……是的，您确实很聪明。 [pc.name]是菲兰德遗产当之无愧的继承者。”娜雷瓦轻声抽泣着，擦去眼角的泪水，“现在再否认也毫无意义了。没错，你说得对，我确实是个幽灵。” 这虽然并非你原本希望听到的真相，但无论如何……一切都结束了。

Yes, you are right. I am a wraith." This wasn't quite the truth you were hoping to uncover, but even so... it's over.'

rows.original: "You are one of them! A wraith!"
rows.translation: 你也是他们中的一员！一个幽灵！
rows.raw: '"You are one of them! A wraith!"'

rows.original: "This is wrong and you know it! You have no right to keep them here!"
rows.translation: 这是不对的，你心里明白这一点！你没有权利把它们留在这里！
rows.raw: '"This is wrong and you know it! You have no right to keep them here!"'

rows.original:
"A fascinating theory, to be sure," Nareva says, shifting her serpentine coils. "But all this conjecture is — "

        "Not so fast. So you're saying that you've been keeping Ander and Ria here for nothing? Given your determination to hold on to them, going as far as to lie and deflect repeatedly... not to speak of the fact that you're always so careful and methodical in the tales, which is only proved by everything I've seen of you so far. Your protestation that you would keep the siblings here when it would be highly inefficient to do so... I cannot trust in the slightest."
        
        "Hmm. Go on, then. Finish that thought."
        
        "That you took the time and care to construct an artifact dedicated to the preservation of memories, ephemeral things that they are — yet at the same time, entrust the whole of mirror magic to the vast intellect of Ander seems somewhat incongruous. This goes doubly so when even you admit even your own memory isn't infallible — what can mere flesh and blood hope to achieve where divinity has failed?"
        
        "You underestimate yourselves at times. The prince here has quite the vast intellect, even if it is often misapplied. That, and he has been in quite the state of blissful stasis for some time until you arrived."
        
        "Even so, you would have known that securing his cooperation in teaching others mirror magic would have been problematic. If only you'd simply used the well, this whole conversation would not need to take place."
        
        "Oh, this conversation has been quite beneficial in and of itself; you would not believe how educational these last couple of centuries have been. Ever since the seven of us incarnated here on this world... we could have left after the Godswar concluded and our duty was discharged, but the sheer joy and interest that interacting with all of you in so direct a fashion led us to stay longer than we ought to."
rows.translation:
确实是一个引人入胜的理论，”纳雷瓦说道，她那蜿蜒盘曲的肢体微微动了动。“但所有这些猜测都只是……”

“别急。那么你是说，你把安德和莉亚关在这里完全是白费力气吗？考虑到你如此坚决地想要留住他们，甚至不惜反复撒谎、转移话题来达到目的。更不用说你在讲述故事时总是那么谨慎、有条理，这一点从我目前所见的一切中已经得到了充分的证明。你声称会把那些兄弟姐妹留在这里，尽管这样做效率极低，但你的这一决定确实体现了你的这种特质。我根本无法信任他们。
        
        嗯，继续说吧。把你的想法说完整。”

“你花费了时间和精力去制造这样一个专门用于保存记忆的物品——毕竟记忆本就是转瞬即逝的东西；然而，同时又将所有的镜像魔法都寄托在安德这样伟大的智慧之上，这似乎有些矛盾。尤其是当你自己也承认自己的记忆并不总是准确的时，这种矛盾就更明显了——对于那些神明都无法做到的事情，区区凡人又怎么可能成功呢？
        
        你们有时确实低估了自己。这位王子其实拥有相当渊博的智慧，只不过这些智慧常常被用错了地方。而且，在你们到来之前，他一直处于一种平静、稳定的状态。”

“即便如此，你们也应该明白，要想让他配合教导别人如何使用镜像魔法，肯定是会遇到麻烦的。如果当初你们直接利用那个井的话，这一切讨论根本就不必要发生。
        
        哦，这次谈话本身就非常有意义；你绝对想不到，过去这几个世纪对我们来说是多么有教育意义。自从我们七个人降临到这个世界上……在神战结束、我们的使命完成之后，我们本可以离开，但与你们所有人进行如此直接的交流所带来的快乐与乐趣，让我们决定留下来更久一些。

rows.original: "That you've another reason for keeping them here."
rows.translation: 这么说，你把它们留在这里还有其他原因。
rows.raw: '"That you\'ve another reason for keeping them here."'

rows.original:
"Nothing? No, no. If you haven't been paying attention to the conversation so far, my dear guest, Ander is here to preserve the legacy of Tychris — mirror magic. Ria is... well, as I said, here to keep him company. It's as simple as that. While I can guess at what you mean, no, I have not been wasting my energy on a less efficient solution to the problem."

        That's... that's right. You really ought to have been paying attention to the conversation, or you'd have known she's covered this argument already. [silly|Pay attention to what people are saying next time, damn it. This is a conversation battle, you're not pressing ahead just to see the scenes.]
rows.translation:
没什么吗？不，不。亲爱的客人，如果你一直没有认真听我们的对话的话，那么安德尔来这里是为了传承提克里斯的遗志——镜像魔法。而莉亚……嗯，就像我之前说的，她只是来陪他的而已。就是这么简单。虽然我能猜到你的意思，但不，我并没有把精力浪费在那些效率更低、效果更差的解决方案上。”

是啊……你真的应该认真听我们的对话，否则你就应该知道她已经把这个问题解释清楚了。 [silly|下次注意别人在说什么吧，真是的。这可是一场对话战斗，你不能只是为了看场景而盲目推进对话啊。]

rows.original: "That you've been keeping them here all for nothing."
rows.translation: 原来你把它们放在这里，完全是在白费力气。
rows.raw: '"That you\'ve been keeping them here all for nothing."'

rows.original:
Nareva shrugs. "If you won't explain yourself when asked a direct question, I suppose we'll have to leave it at that. Are we done with this conversation?"

        "Wait! No! I just needed to gather my thoughts to form a proper answer."
        
        "You're not stupid or slow-witted, or you wouldn't have gotten this far. I'd like to think I can tell when someone's stalling for time, trying to find a straw to grasp at. None of this nonsense, please."
        
        Like it or not, she's right. You can't afford any improper delays in the conversation like this, not when she's playing hard defense and finding any excuse to avoid talking to you.
rows.translation:
纳雷瓦耸了耸肩：“如果别人直接问你问题，你却不愿意解释，那我想我们就只能到此为止了。我们的谈话结束了吗？”

“等等！不是这样的！我只是需要稍微整理一下思路，才能给出一个合适的回答而已。你既不愚蠢，也不迟钝，否则也不可能走到这一步。我认为自己能够分辨出别人是在拖延时间、在试图找些借口来应对问题。请别再搞这些无聊的把戏了。不管你愿不愿意承认，她是对的。在这种情况下，你绝对不能允许任何不必要的拖延，尤其是当她正在极力抵抗、想方设法逃避与你交谈的时候。
rows.raw:
"
        Nareva shrugs. "If you won't explain yourself when asked a direct question, I suppose we'll have to leave it at that. Are we done with this conversation?"

        "Wait! No! I just needed to gather my thoughts to form a proper answer."
        
        "You're not stupid or slow-witted, or you wouldn't have gotten this far. I'd like to think I can tell when someone's stalling for time, trying to find a straw to grasp at. None of this nonsense, please."
        
        Like it or not, she's right. You can't afford any improper delays in the conversation like this, not when she's playing hard defense and finding any excuse to avoid talking to you."

rows.original: Remain silent and observe the situation.
rows.translation: 保持沉默，观察事态的发展。

rows.original:
"Alas. Whatever shall I do in the face of criticism so scathing. Well then, since this is all so unpleasant for you, why don't we just end the conversation here and call it quits? You can wake up none the wiser, and your life will be just as droll as it was before."

        "Alas, unpleasant as it is, I have to stick through it for Ander and Ria's sake."
        
        A lazy shrug. "You're not doing yourself any favors by being deliberately antagonistic, at any rate. Keep it up, and I might just decide to evict you anyway. Now, where were we...?"
rows.translation:
唉，面对如此尖锐的批评，我该怎么办呢？既然这一切让你如此不快，那我们就就此结束这次谈话吧，算了吧。你醒来后依然会一无所知，你的生活也会和之前一样无聊。唉，虽然这很令人不快，但为了安德和莉亚，我不得不坚持下去。”

他懒洋洋地耸了耸肩：“反正，你故意惹人嫌，并不会对自己有什么好处。如果你继续这样，我可能会决定把你赶出去。 现在，我们刚才说到哪里了……？
rows.raw:
'
        "Alas. Whatever shall I do in the face of criticism so scathing. Well then, since this is all so unpleasant for you, why don't we just end the conversation here and call it quits? You can wake up none the wiser, and your life will be just as droll as it was before."

        "Alas, unpleasant as it is, I have to stick through it for Ander and Ria's sake."
        
        A lazy shrug. "You're not doing yourself any favors by being deliberately antagonistic, at any rate. Keep it up, and I might just decide to evict you anyway. Now, where were we...?"'

rows.original: "I'm experiencing neither joy nor interest interacting with you right now."
rows.translation: 目前，与你交流并没有给我带来任何快乐或兴趣。
rows.raw: '"I\'m experiencing neither joy nor interest interacting with you right now."'

rows.original:
"Yes and no. The Godswar was a valid reason for direct intervention, since without us deities stepping in the odds of your survival were not good, to put it lightly. But afterwards... well, all of us have differing opinions on exactly how much personal interaction we should have with the various mortal races. Lumia loves to meddle with her so-called children every chance she gets. Some, like me, have taken up patronage of a nation, or perhaps a people, and content ourselves with having a limited hand, but even so..."

        "Yes?"
        
        "Personally speaking, as joyful as my experiences with them might have been, I have tried to limit my direct interactions with the en Tychris line ever since Philander's father passed. I did not want them to come running to me with every problem they had, seeking a solution; it would only stunt their rebuilding efforts and encourage dependency. Yet at the same time I had to have enough of a presence to mark them as claimed territory after a fashion, lest another of the Seven think it ripe ground for proselytisation."
        
        "Let me guess," you say. "Even if it's a useful tool, you don't want to become reliant on the Well in the same fashion you don't want your devotees to become reliant on you."
        
        Nareva smiles almost patronisingly. "See? I knew you could work it out for yourself. Even in this day there are some tribes of orcs and centaurs that are illiterate... they have beautiful oral traditions, passed down by word of mouth and seared into the mind with interesting mnemonic techniques. Simple literacy was an extremely useful tool, but in becoming reliant on it, peoples' capabilities unfortunately degenerated... someday, I would like to capture those particular secrets before they finally vanish from the world. Either way, I try to only use the Well of Memory in this fashion when there is some detail I cannot afford to lose — and as annoying as this situation is, it certainly is not enough to warrant its use. Do you now understand why I cannot release the siblings?"
rows.translation:
可以说是，也可以说不是。‘神战’确实是一个让我们直接介入的正当理由，因为如果没有我们这些神明的干预，你们这些凡人的生存几率可以说非常渺茫。但之后……嗯，对于我们应该与各个凡人种族保持多大的互动程度，我们大家的意见其实并不一致。 卢米娅一有机会就喜欢干涉她那些所谓的“孩子们”。其中有些人，比如我，选择扶持某个国家或某个民族，满足于发挥有限的影响力；但即便如此……

        是吗？”

“就我个人而言，尽管与他们在一起的那些经历非常愉快，但在菲兰德的父亲去世后，我就尽量减少了与恩·提克里斯家族的直接接触。我不想让他们一遇到问题就跑来找我寻求解决办法；那样只会阻碍他们的重建工作，还会让他们产生依赖心理。 然而，与此同时，我必须展现出足够的影响力，以便将这些地区视为自己的势力范围——否则，其他七位成员中的某位可能会认为这些地方是传播自己理念的理想场所。
        
        让我猜猜看，”你说，“即使这是一个有用的工具，你也不想变得过于依赖它，就如同你不希望你的追随者们也变得依赖你一样。”

纳雷瓦几乎带着一种居高临下的姿态笑了起来。 看吧？我就知道你能自己想出办法来。即使在今天，也还是有一些兽人族群和半人马族群不识字……但他们拥有精美的口述传统，这些传统通过口口相传的方式传承下来，并且通过一些有趣的记忆技巧被牢牢地记在人们的脑海中。 基本的读写能力确实是一种极其有用的工具，但人们一旦过于依赖它，他们的能力反而会退化……有朝一日，我希望能将这些珍贵的秘密记录下来，以免它们最终从这个世界消失。 无论如何，我只会在这种必须保留某些关键细节的情况下才会使用“记忆之井”——尽管这种情况确实很烦人，但还不足以成为使用它的理由。现在你明白为什么我不能释放那些兄弟姐妹了吧？"

rows.original: "'Ought to'? Was there some reason you shouldn't have stayed?"
rows.translation: 应该’吗？难道有什么原因让你不能留下来吗？
rows.raw: "\"'Ought to'? Was there some reason you shouldn't have stayed?\""

rows.original:
"So, you have no reply? Doing the smart thing and finally giving it a rest? This verbal tussle has dragged on for so long, it's frankly quite tiring..."

        "You could end it too by simply giving in."
        
        "Ah, but then I would be betraying the responsibility placed upon me by virtue of my station. That would be quite the gross dereliction of duty, wouldn't it?"
        
        "So it seems we must continue."
        
        "If you must. Do try and waste less time while going about it."
rows.translation:
所以，你还是没有答案吗？终于决定放弃这场无谓的争论了？这场口角已经持续了太久，说实话，真的让人感到疲惫……”

“你也可以通过简单地让步来结束这一切。”

“啊，但是那样我就违背了我所肩负的责任。那可就是严重的失职行为了，不是吗？”

“看来我们还得继续下去。”

“如果你非得这样的话……那就尽量别再浪费时间了。

        "You could end it too by simply giving in."

rows.original:
"I can't help but notice something quite troublesome with your argument, though," you say. "Just now you attempted to make a point by calling into question the prince's ability to recall everyone he had invited to the convocation, something he had done not that long ago by his reckoning."

        "..."
        
        "Now, you're trying to claim that he has had, and will continue to retain picture-perfect memory of his magic over how long you intend to keep him here. I find this contradiction quite unsettling, especially since the duty associated with your station hinges on it. If Ander has lost one iota of what he knows about mirror magic while in your care... you'll have failed to preserve the knowledge of a form of magic by trying to keep secrets."
        
        "...So that's why they're so interested in you. Truly, a fine eye for details... not that I would have expected anything else."
        
        "That selfsame duty," you add, "which you claim drives you to such lengths and requires you to deal with so much unpleasantness. This rather lackadaisical approach is yet another issue with your argument."
        
        "...What are you insinuating here?"

不过，我不得不指出你的论点中存在一些相当棘手的问题，”你说。“刚才你试图通过质疑王子是否能够记住他邀请来参加这次会议的所有人来支持你的观点，而按照你的说法，王子就在不久前还做过这件事。……

"Tenacious and determined, if nothing else, with an eye for the fine details. Virtues that unfortunately are in the wrong place at the wrong time."

        "I'll take that as a compliment, then."
        
        "It was. Which is why all this is such a waste." Nareva sighs and makes a show of yawning. "Oh, by the by, trying to stall for time is most unbecoming of you."
        
        "I wasn't — "
        
        "It was either that, or you just knowingly meandered off onto a complete non-sequitur. Given what I've figured out about you, the former is more likely. Can we avoid wasting time like this? Even if there's no rush, I do find myself growing irritated..."

坚韧不拔、意志坚定，而且注重细节——这些品质，可惜在错误的时间出现在了错误的人身上。”

        Hmm... aggravating her here might not have been the best of ideas. Provoking Nareva when she's clearly on guard isn't going to yield you any results. You're so close to the truth now, you can't afford to fail at this point!

"Well then, you've fallen silent. Does that mean you've finally realized the wisdom of letting sleeping dogs lie?"

        You grin. "Hah. I was just pondering how to get a reticent goddess to spill the beans."
        
        "Stalling for time and grasping at straws isn't going to do you any good, my dear guest. You can keep on running in circles, but are you going to get anywhere?"
        
        [var0
            |Well, then. Looks like that's a challenge to reveal what you do know — perhaps it's time to use that clue, then...
            |Damn it, you've come thus far, but she's right.         ]

rows.original:
"Just now... when I brought up the topic of traitors, you had a rather visceral reaction and said quite a number of things. It leads me to wonder if — "

            "None of that's true! I — I'm not — "
            
            Looking at Nareva, her ophidian coils agitated, fangs bared, bosom heaving as she gasps for breath — you know you've hit the mark here. Even so... she looks more ashamed than angry. "You're not... what, exactly? Did you betray someone? Does that have something to do with why you're keeping Ander and Ria in here with you?"
            
            "...Isn't it enough? Can't it be enough? More than two centuries I've worked, trying to undo the damage of that day, repay what I've taken. Can't you just give it a rest? Why do you have to hound me like this? Doesn't everything I've done for Tychris count for anything?"
            
            You're watching a goddess throw a tearful tantrum. Will wonders never cease. But thinking about what she's just said... 
            
            ...What did she take? If she was repaying Tychris all this time... 
            
            Wait. It can't be. But it's the only thread of thought that makes sense... and if that's true, then it puts everything that Nareva's told you in a completely different light. You thought she might have betrayed Tychris, but this turns things around completely.
            
            If this is the truth she was trying to hide... it is an unpalatable one. No wonder she was trying to hide it.
            
            ...She was right, after all. You... you might just come to regret knowing this. Either way, you've finally wrenched open the heavy door to the truth. All that remains now... is to deal the final blow.

"Of course," Nareva replies. "Know your enemy and know yourself, and you will emerge victorious every time; know neither your enemy nor yourself, and defeat is certain. In order to effectively fight the wraiths, I had to know their capabilities well, and impart that knowledge to anyone who was willing to fight them. The extent of the fate that awaits their victims only scratches the surface of what there is to know."
        
        "And did they have favorite kinds of victims, the same way we have favorite foods, or did they just start from the outside and eat their way in?"
        
        "Hmm. Probably, but to one who has never tasted anything before, even water is like wine. They may have had favorites, but thinking about it, everything was attractive enough that I imagine they were content to consume indiscriminately."
        
        "Odd, then, that they didn't consume Sigrune. As mighty as she was as a jotun, I imagine the wraiths would have been easily able to overpower her."
        
        "It was decided to leave Sigrune alive. Her standing guard at the archway for all time would have certainly delayed news of the convocation's fate from spreading — not that it mattered, since the wraiths clearly didn't count on my arrival on the scene."

“那么，它们有没有自己偏爱的受害者类型，就像我们会有喜欢的食物一样？还是说，它们只是从外部开始，然后逐渐深入到内部去捕食呢？嗯，大概吧。但对于那些从未尝过任何东西的人来说，就连水也像酒一样美味。他们可能会有自己喜欢的饮品，但仔细想想，所有这些食物都应该都足够诱人，因此我想他们应该会毫无选择地享用它们吧。那么，他们没有吞噬西格鲁娜，这就很奇怪了。毕竟她作为乔顿族的一员，实力如此强大，我想那些幽灵应该很容易就能制服她才对。”

“最终，人们决定让西格鲁娜活下来。 她一直守在拱门处，这无疑延缓了关于这次集会命运的消息的传播——不过这也无关紧要，因为那些幽灵显然没有预料到我会出现在现场。

rows.original: "You seem to know a lot about wraith predation. Could you elaborate?"
rows.translation: 你似乎对‘怨灵捕食’这一现象了解得很多。能详细讲讲吗？
rows.raw: '"You seem to know a lot about wraith predation. Could you elaborate?"'

rows.original:
"So as you can see," Nareva continues, "my options were few; much of the damage had already been done. At some point, you have to realize that it's not just an untreatable injury, but the poor bastard is already dead."

        "This answer doesn't sit right with me," Ria mutters, folding her arms.
        
        "Neither does it for me," you add.
        
        Nareva shrugs and sighs. "As it shouldn't. After all, Phyria, you were responsible for security at your half-brother's little party; this failure must sting more than you're willing to acknowledge. Yet matters were what they were — I know that your mother trained you to never admit that there was nothing that could have been done to improve a situation, but sometimes that is just the case.
        
        "In any case, that concludes what I have to say on the matter. Are you satisfied?"
        
        You shake your head. "No, not quite yet. There're still some more things I have to ask."
        
        "Oh dear, can't you give it a rest? This conversation is really starting to drag, and you're getting nowhere..."<i/>

rows.original: You frown. "Decided? Who exactly made the decision?" "Why, the wraiths, of course. Who else?" "Which is my point. If the wraiths made the conscious decision to leave Sigrune alive, then how did you know that? It doesn't sound like the sort of information they'd share with an enemy." Nareva frowns. "Wraiths aren't mindless animals, [pc.name]. They may lack any sense of morality or conscience, but certainly have an intelligence of their own. Don't underestimate them — they're certainly capable of making decisions and planning ahead. Even animals are capable of that, albeit in limited capacity. Knowing that, I simply worked back from their actions, and it was the only explanation that made sense." "So there might have been another reason why Sigrune was spared? You sounded so confident there..." "I'm confident in my judgement, yes. Given the state of the situation, it was the only reasonable explanation — what were you expecting, that Sigrune simply didn't taste good?"

rows.original: "If only, if only. If only the prince had chosen another location for his convocation. If only the wraiths had chosen to take Sigrune as an appetiser before the main course. If only everyone hadn't been asleep when it all happened. If only there'd been an alternative path off the plateau. There were so many details that could've changed the outcome of that day, my dear guest, but it's pointless to speculate now that it's long done and over with." "I'm not so sure about that." "Speculation sometimes does have a purpose, but doing so wildly in the hopes of apportioning blame or concocting fantasies of alternate outcomes for an event long past isn't something I'm fond of, just so you know. Not that I enjoy wasting time in general. If we're going to allow the conversation to devolve into unfounded threads, why don't we just cut it off?" Damn it, she's trying to run away, and you're not about to let her, not when you're so close to the truth now! Like it or not, you need to ask relevant questions that are concretely based on what she said and she can't snake her way out of.

rows.original:
"There we have it. Are you satisfied with my answer, my dear guest?"

        You think about it for a second. Sure, she's answered your question about wraiths, but there're a million more you'd like to ask, especially from someone who was there for much of the Godswar... "I can't deny you've answered it, although whether it's in full is another matter."
        
        "I suppose you have cause to doubt me at this point, but even so, unless you can say with certainty I'm not speaking the truth..."
        
        Yes, yes, you get it. You've heard this song and dance before. Maybe you should've pressed her somewhere else in that line of conversation... but for now, the opportunity is lost. You'll need to get back to where you were and try again.
rows.translation:
就是这样。我的亲爱的客人，您对我的回答满意吗？”

请稍作思考。当然，她确实回答了您关于幽灵的问题，但您肯定还有无数其他问题想要问，尤其是对于一个亲身经历了整个神战的人来说。我不得不承认你已经回答了这个问题，不过你的回答是否完整，那就是另一回事了。”

“我想在这个时候，你确实有理由怀疑我，但即便如此，除非你能确定我说的是假话，否则还是不能这样认为。……”

“是的，是的，你明白我的意思。这种话你以前也听过很多次了。也许在刚才的对话中，你应该选择在其他地方提问……但现在机会已经错过了。你得回到刚才的地方，再试一次。

rows.original: "Well then, do you have a better one? No, let me retract that — it's perfectly valid to criticise something without having an alternative at hand. Whether that criticism has any valid grounding, though..." "You're one to speak, considering that I've caught you lying quite a few times now." "Ah, I was there, and you were not; I am privy to information that you are not. Oh, and by the by, I have yet to hear why you think the explanation is insufficient. No, disliking me is not a valid reason." ...Damn it, there she goes again. While you're sure that Nareva is being deceptive somewhere, you need to press her on things that you can actually prove. Having come so far, shouldn't you know this by now?

rows.original:
Ria scowls and prods you on the back right between the shoulders. "This isn't the time for joking, [pc.name]! Ander and I are counting on you to get us out of this snake-witch's hands, and here you are — "

        "I don't know, sister. Sigrune's always in such a foul mood that I'd expect her to taste bitter, if not ashen."
        
        Ria glares daggers at her half-brother, then groans and holds her head in her hands. For all her strength and brazen willpower, the poor 'mander is clearly reaching the end of her tether here.
        
        The whole exchange has Nareva quietly tut-tutting away. "The attempt at levity is noted, but Ria has the right of it. Let's avoid stalling for time, shall we? If you've got nothing left but to grasp at straws, then perhaps we should put this conversation to a close."
rows.translation:
莉亚皱着眉头，在你右肩后面轻轻戳了你一下：“现在不是开玩笑的时候。 [pc.name]安德尔和我都指望你能帮我们摆脱这个女巫的掌控，而你现在终于出现了——”

“我不知道，姐姐。西格鲁娜总是心情糟糕透顶，所以我猜她现在应该气得够呛，甚至可能会气得脸色发灰吧。
        
        莉亚恶狠狠地瞪了她的同父异母的弟弟一眼，然后呻吟着双手部抱住了头。尽管她拥有强大的体力和坚定的意志力，但这个可怜的女孩显然已经到了忍无可忍的地步。

在整个过程中，娜雷瓦一直在默默地发出啧啧声。 虽然她试图用轻松的方式打破气氛，但她的做法也是情有可原的。我们还是不要浪费时间了，好吗？如果你已经没有任何其他办法，只能徒劳地抓救命稻草的话，那么或许我们应该结束这次谈话了。

rows.translation: 我敢打赌，那些幽灵肯定会觉得她的味道非常难吃。

rows.original:
"Right," Nareva continues after a moment's silence. "Despite their eager hunger and amoral nature, stories that have no doubt grown in the telling over the years, wraiths are not stupid creatures. Many learned that lesson the hard way."

        "They must have been terrible foes to face."
        
        "There are a number of reasons the Godswar lasted as long as it did. The strength of those who opposed us was one of them. Many native populations about the world were subsumed into the wraiths' hosts... morsels of power with the promise of more to come were sufficient to turn the easily swayed to their side. Perhaps they thought they ought to get in good with the winning team while they could, and their logic would not have been without merit."
        
        "It sounds like you're trying to make these traitors to their own world appear sympathetic."
        
        "Well, you must understand it from their point of view. Monsters from the void between the worlds show up, make an example of your neighbors, then offer you power or a fate worse than death. Given such extenuating circumstances, saying no is hard; not all people are made of strong moral fiber. Knowing all this, I was slightly more lenient in passing judgement when the time came... I am quite merciful, after all. More than Tira, at any rate."
        
        "You seem rather familiar with all this..."
        
        "..."

“想必，它们一定是极其可怕的敌人吧。
        
        Godswar能够持续这么长时间，其中原因有很多。那些与我们对抗的力量也是其中之一。世界上许多原住民都被卷入了那些幽灵的势力之中……那些许的力量，以及未来还会得到更多利益的承诺，足以让那些容易受影响的人站到他们那一边。或许他们认为，趁现在还来得及，应该与胜利的一方建立良好的关系，而他们的这种逻辑也并非毫无道理。
        
        听起来你是在试图让这些背叛自己世界的家伙显得有点可同情之处。”

“嗯，你必须从他们的角度来理解这件事。那些来自世界间隙的怪物出现了，先杀了你的邻居作为警告，然后要么给你力量，要么赐予你比死亡更可怕的命运。 考虑到这样的特殊情况，拒绝别人确实是一件很难的事——毕竟，并不是每个人都能具备坚定的道德准则。了解了这些之后，当真正需要做出判断的时候，我也就稍微宽容了一些……毕竟，我也是一个相当仁慈的人。 至少比蒂拉还要多。
        
        你似乎对这一切都非常熟悉……”

That snaps Nareva out of her reverie, her ophidian features reasserting themselves into their usual guarded expression. "I was considering the distant past."

        "And that is?"
        
        "Nothing relating to the conversation. Simply something Phyria's mother said to me, which is not my secret to share. Perhaps with Phyria, but not with you."
        
        "That's awfully convenient and evasive to boot."
        
        "And yet I will still refuse to give it up."
        
        Damn, you've put her on guard, and she's stonewalling you now. All talking is going to do now is take you in circles; you really shouldn't interrupt an opponent in the middle of making a mistake.
rows.translation:
这声话语将纳雷瓦从她的沉思中惊醒，她那蛇一般的面容又恢复了惯常的警惕神情。“我在思考遥远的过去。”

“那么，你想到了什么？”

“与这次谈话无关的事情。 这只是菲莉亚的母亲对我说过的话，并非什么需要分享的秘密。或许可以告诉菲莉亚，但不会告诉你。

“这种说法未免太方便了，同时也太含糊其辞了。”

“不过，我还是拒绝透露这个秘密。该死，你把她惹得提高了警惕，现在她开始故意拖延、拒绝配合你了。再继续这样下去，只会让谈话陷入僵局；其实，在对手犯错的时候，你根本不应该去打断他们。

rows.original: Nareva stares at you. You return the stare. At last, she speaks again. "Like I said before, I had to be. Strength is one thing, but with knowledge to direct it, its efficacy is multiplied manifold. Knowing what the wraiths' followers wanted out of the whole deal allowed us to undermine their will to fight, so that the battle was over before it even started. Of course, since they'd already turned once, they were never allowed critical roles or positions of authority." "Traitors, huh?" "Traitors... they're strange things. Even when they defect for a good cause, even knowing they were coerced, and quite strongly in a good number of cases... they're still not to be trusted. Someone who has turned once always leaves the possibility they could be turned again. Zealots who have been disillusioned often don't become moderates, they simply find another cause to fight for, with the same fervor. Sometimes, I find that even as a goddess, I have so much more in common with you mortals than I could ever imagine. It's that joy of simple discovery, not just about the world but about myself, that's helped keep me going all this while. Amongst other things, of course." "Hmm." Now that's interesting. Nareva certainly grew contentious when the subject of traitors and defectors came up... the subject is clearly touchy to her. While the goddess is clearly suppressing her emotions, those evoked by the topic were strong enough to break through her facade... That might be an important clue.
rows.translation: 纳雷瓦注视着你，你也回望着她。终于，她再次开口：“就像我之前说的，我必须这么做。力量是一回事，但如果有知识来引导它，它的效力就会成倍增加。了解那些幽灵的追随者们从整个计划中想要得到什么，让我们能够削弱他们战斗的意志，这样这场战斗甚至还没开始就已经结束了。当然，由于他们曾经背叛过一次，所以我们从未允许他们担任任何关键角色或拥有权威职位。 叛徒，哈？” “叛徒……他们真是奇怪的存在。即使他们是因为正义的理由而背叛，即使他们知道自己是被胁迫的，而且在很多情况下，这种胁迫力相当大……他们仍然不可信任。 那些曾经转变过立场的人，总是会留下再次改变的可能性。那些曾经幻想破灭的狂热分子，往往并不会变得温和，他们只是会找到另一个值得为之奋斗的目标，依然以同样的热情去投身其中。有时候，我甚至会意识到，即使身为一位女神，我和你们这些凡人之间其实有着许多我此前从未想象过的共同点。 正是这种简单的发现所带来的快乐——不仅仅是对这个世界的认识，更是对我自身的了解——才让我能够坚持下去。当然，还有其他许多因素也在其中起到了作用。 嗯。”这确实很有意思。每当提到叛徒和变节者的时候，纳雷瓦的反应总是很激烈……这个话题显然让她非常敏感。虽然这位女神一直在努力压抑自己的情绪，但这个话题引发的那些情绪却强烈到足以突破她的伪装…… 那可能是一个重要的线索。

rows.original: You could make a genuine, bold attempt to evade the corrupted lupines. Or, if you're feeling a little... mischievous, you could pretend to run away and then let them catch you once they're all good and worked up.
rows.translation: 你 可以 你可以认真而大胆地尝试躲避那些被腐蚀的狼族。当然，如果你觉得有点……调皮的话，也可以假装逃跑，等它们全都追上来、兴奋不已的时候，再让它们抓住你。

rows.original: But it is not enough. Despite your best efforts of sweat and ardor, you're unable to shake the pursuit of these manic wolfmen. Whatever success you may gain is only ever temporary. The distance between the pack and you is gradually shrinking at an ever-accelerating rate and so is your hope of escaping. On all fours, the hysteric hunter digs his claws into the soil and flexes his muscles as he braces for a pouncing leap. Then, like a twisted coil finally unleashed, the manic springs forward in a sailing lunge through the air. The sheer momentous force, in which his bulky frame collides into you, sends the two of you tumbling to the ground. Tackled harshly to the forest's floor, you try not to focus on the stinging bruise. It hurts, but your mind is preoccupied with the frantic rush of instinct. It's fight or flight and, at this juncture, running is no longer an option. You have to escape this grapple!

rows.original: Swing upon swing, the blows of your fists ineffectively cushion against the tainted lupine's thick, matted fur and firmly packed muscles; furthermore, past the physical weight of his body over you and past the fatigue setting in, you detect the presence of something else. rows.translation: 切身感受到体力的衰退， [party.som |你 |你和你的另一位同伴 |你和你的同伴们 ] 当那一群堕落的狼群逐渐逼近你时，你拼命想要站稳脚跟。它们扭曲的脸上露出了凶残的笑容。你毫无办法阻止它们，两只饥渴的猎犬径直冲向你的物品。它们撕碎你的背包，抢走一切能抓到的东西，无论是补给品，还是你辛苦赚来的电银。 [var0 | 在这些拾荒者翻找你的背包时，他们终于找到了自己想要的东西。凭借“征服权”，他们将你的食物和补给据为己有。对于这群被腐蚀了的野兽来说，它们与同伴之间的合作程度令人惊讶——它们会公平地分享这些物资，而不会像野蛮的狗一样为争夺食物而互相争斗。 | 他们在你的包里翻来翻去，却并没有找到他们想要的东西。这些小家伙互相吠叫、咆哮着，似乎在交流些什么，然后又再次翻找你的物品栏。为了弥补他们没有得到的东西，它们便以“征服者”的身份，索要了比最初更多的硬币作为补偿。 | 他们在你的包里翻来翻去，却一次也没有找到他们想要的东西。一次……两次……三次，他们反复检查你的物品清单。每次这样的尝试都会让他们变得更加愤怒。他们怒火中烧，每个人都…… 刺眼的光线 就看你的了。不管怎样，他们总会拿到他们应得的东西。如果得不到食物，他们也很乐意攻击你的自尊心来作为替代品。 ] 三名成员中有两人离开后，便四肢着地，朝着荒野深处冲了出去。这样一来，就只剩下…… [party.yall] 它们中的最后一只狼看着同伴一个个离开，然后漫不经心地嗅了嗅空气，耸了耸肩，又将注意力重新转向你。当这只野兽朝你的方向走来时，你突然意识到——它们还没有结束对你的追击。 战利品. rows.original:
You [pc.HPDefeated
        |feel the keen loss of vigor
        |pant lustfully
    ] and fall to your knees as the pack of corrupted lupines slowly encroach upon [party.yall]. A predatory grin forms on their twisted expressions. Defenseless to stop the beastmen, two of them grab your arms and motion to drag you away.
    
    Cait sees what's happening and musters what remains of her determination in order to stand back up. Left with no better options, she performs a last ditch effort to protect [party.manyCompanions
        |the group
        |you
    ].
    
    [var0
        |"Close your eyes!" Cait shouts.
        
        Hastily, you heed her request and shield your eyes as she summons forth the light of the Jassiran sun. As a result, the wolfmen let you go, and you slump face-first onto the forest floor.
        |"Get your hands off of [pc.himHer]!" Cait shouts in defiance, her figurative hackles raised towards the burly wolfmen. She then raises her [cait.weapon] and channels a barrier of force around you, creating a scintillating bubble that's as hard as armor and soothing as a lover's kiss. "[party.manyCompanions
            |Take [companion2.name] and get
            |Get
        ] out of here! I'll hold them off."
        |Cait channels thunderous power into her weapon and charges toward a corrupted lupine, making a show of divine wrath as she sends him flying with an explosive blast of argent energy. "Who's next?" She points her weapon to the pair of lupines holding you and says, "If you want to get to [pc.himHer], you'll have to go through me."
        
        The wolfmen let go of you and direct their attention to Cait. Slowly, they get on all fours and circle around the pink spellblade, waiting for the right opportunity to strike. After a few seconds, the one she struck gets back up and joins the others in flanking her.
        
        Cait stands her ground and braces for an attack that could come from any direction. She then turns to you and shouts, "[party.manyCompanions
            |Take [companion2.name] and get
            |Get
        ] out of here! Don't worry, I'll hold them off."
        |"Forgetting someone?" Cait purrs. Slowly, she throws herself into a lascivious dance, putting everything on display as she shakes her hips at the corrupted lupines — clothing falls away to reveal bare, tempting flesh for all to see. And, judging by the hungry look in their eyes, her little performance seems to have been a success in commanding their attention away from [party.manyCompanions
            |the rest of the group
            |you
        ].
        
        The wolfmen ogle Cait's sumptuous form and lick their jagged fangs as they slowly approach her. Now's your chance to escape and recuperate. You look to your cat-companion for confirmation and she returns with a silent nod as she's surrounded by the burly wolf trio.
        |"Get your hands off of [pc.himHer]!" She shouts in defiance, her figurative hackles raised toward the burly wolfmen "If you want to [party.manyCompanions
            |hurt my friends
            |take [pc.himHer]
        ], you'll have to go through me. Or are you too chicken to fight a [cait.isLeothran
            |big, fluffy kitty
            |little lady
        ]?"
    ]
    
    Taking your cue, you[party.manyCompanions
        | and [companion2.name]
    ] grab your things and put some distance between you and the enemy. Eventually, you[party.manyCompanions
        | and [companion2.name]
    ] pause to rest in a small clearing in the Old Forest. Despite having to flee, you're not going to abandon Cait. That simply isn't going to happen. She's [pc.isDK
        |still a valuable asset
        |been with you since the beginning
    ]. Unfortunately, as of right now, [party.manyCompanions
        |the two of you are
        |you're
    ] in no condition to keep fighting. Cait's a strong girl, but she's only one person against three sex-hungry beasts. It's not hard to imagine what the wolfmen are going to do to Cait when they get their hands on her. Make no mistake, you're going back for her; you just need to [pc.HPDefeated
        |regain your strength
        |recompose yourself
    ] first. Question is: are you going to risk heading back, or should you just sit here and stage a rescue when [party.manyCompanions
        |everyone is
        |you're
    ] good and ready?
